news.Title: Earnings live updates: Moderna's COVID vaccine sales drive revenue growth, raised outlook
news.Content:
The third quarter earnings season is over halfway done, and the reports continue to pour in. This week brought another shot of major earnings courtesy of Apple ( AAPL ), Palantir ( PLTR ), and AMD ( AMD ).

In addition to those tech heavyweights, investors are watching the results out of Roku ( ROKU ), Arm Holdings ( ARM ), McDonald's ( MCD ), QUALCOMM ( QCOM ), Novo Nordisk ( NVO ), Uber Technologies ( UBER ), Toyota Motor Corporation ( TM ), ConocoPhillips ( COP ), and Moderna ( MRNA ).

S&P 500 corporations continue to demonstrate robust earnings growth. According to FactSet data , approximately 60% of S&P 500 companies have already reported Q3 earnings, with an overall earnings growth rate of 30.2%. If that rate holds, it will mark the third straight quarter of earnings growth above 25% for the index.

LIVE 14 updates

24 mins ago Grace O'Donnell

Moderna posts first profit in 2 years

Moderna ( MRNA ) just posted its first profit in two years. The stock fluctuated in premarket trading.

In the third quarter, Moderna reported earnings per share of $0.38, beating Wall Street analysts' projection for a $1.25 loss per share. Revenue of $1.3 billion grew 29% year over year also easily surpassed the Street's estimate of $890 million.

Moderna said COVID-19 vaccine sales overseas drove the revenue gains.

"We delivered 29% revenue growth in the third quarter, alongside the U.S. approval of mFLUSIVA, our fifth approved product globally, and positive Phase 3 results for intismeran in melanoma," CEO Stéphane Bancel said.

Moderna raised its full-year revenue guidance. The company now expects sales to grow 15% to 25%, up from its previous outlook of up to 10% growth.

Year-to-date, Moderna stock has surged over 700%, in part due to the positive response to the successful trial of its skin cancer vaccine.

Thu, November 5, 2026 at 10:09 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell

Atlassian tumbles 16% on weaker subscription growth outlook

Investing.com reports:

Atlassian Corporation shares plunged 16% despite the company reporting first-quarter results that topped analyst expectations, as its subscription growth outlook disappointed investors.

The collaboration software provider reported adjusted earnings per share of $1.65, beating analyst estimates of $1.43 by $0.22. Revenue rose 24% year-over-year to $1.77 billion from $1.43 billion a year earlier, surpassing the consensus estimate of $1.71 billion. Adjusted operating margin also came in ahead of expectations at 32%, compared with the estimated 28.6%.

However, investors focused on signs of slowing subscription growth. Atlassian forecast subscription annual recurring revenue (ARR) growth of approximately 18.5% year-over-year for fiscal 2027, down from the 23% growth reported in the first quarter.

Thu, November 5, 2026 at 10:06 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell

Airbnb 'back in growth mode,' CEO says after strong quarter. Stock jumps after hours.

Airbnb ( ABNB ) stock jumped 11% after hours after the peer-to-peer home rental company touted strong growth across its business and raised its full-year outlook amid healthy global travel demand.

"Airbnb is back in growth mode," CEO Brian Chesky said in a release to investors. "It's rare for a marketplace of our size to reaccelerate growth, but that's exactly what we're doing. In Q3, we delivered our fastest revenue growth in more than three years, with acceleration across our business, including our most established markets."

In the third quarter, Airbnb reported earnings per share of $3.16, surpassing Wall Street analyst estimates of $2.85 per share, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence data. Revenue grew 19% to $4.87 billion, also beating estimates of $4.74 billion.

"In North America, nights booked grew at their fastest pace in four years," the company said. "We're also seeing more guests return to Airbnb, and more people try it for the first time."

The strength of the company's quarter led it to raise its guidance for the remainder of the year.

In the fourth quarter, Airbnb expects revenue to grow 16%-19% to a range of $3.22 billion to $3.28 billion, exceeding the Street's midpoint estimate of $3.16 billion.

For the full year, Airbnb forecasts revenue growth in the high teens and adjusted EBITDA margins to increase to approximately 36%.

Thu, November 5, 2026 at 9:52 PM UTC Brooke DiPalma

Bob's Furniture stock rises after better-than-expected results: 'Value is always in vogue'

Bob's Furniture ( BOBS ) reported better-than-expected third quarter results. Revenue came in at $680 million, higher than the $666 million estimates, per Bloomberg consensus data. Adjusted earnings per share also beat estimates by $0.02, coming in at $0.28.

The results were largely driven by customers leaning into higher-cost furniture, with CEO Bill Barton telling Yahoo Finance, "Value is always in vogue."

"The industry continues to struggle, although we think ... the furniture industry stabilized a bit in the third quarter. We're not really calling for a turn yet, ... [but] the trend that we saw in the spring of our customers trading up into the premium price tiers continued in the third quarter. So we saw that average order value going up, and that's really what carried a lot of the comp growth for the third quarter," Barton said.

The company reaffirmed its 2026 guidance, with expectations for same-store sales to grow in the range of 1.5% to 2.5%, but it didn't update its guidance, with Barton calling it a "very dynamic backdrop."

Wed, November 4, 2026 at 9:23 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell

Qualcomm tops Q4 estimates, but Q1 earnings outlook falls short

Yahoo Finance's Dan Howley reports:

Qualcomm ( QCOM ) reported fourth quarter earnings after the bell Wednesday, topping expectations on the top and bottom lines and providing a better-than-anticipated Q1 revenue outlook.

But a lower-than-expected midpoint for its earnings per share (EPS) forecast send shares lower following the report.

For Q4, Qualcomm reported adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of $2.17 on revenue of $10.32 billion. Analysts were projecting EPS of $2.16 and revenue of $10.12 billion.

The company saw EPS of $3.00 and revenue of $11.27 billion in the same quarter last year.

Qualcomm also offered Q1 revenue guidance of $10.4 billion to $11.2 billion, with the midpoint ahead of Wall Street's $10.6 billion outlook.

EPS, though, is set to come in between $2.15 and $2.35 with a midpoint of $2.25. Analysts were looking for $2.32

Wed, November 4, 2026 at 9:18 PM UTC Brooke DiPalma

Cava results fall just shy of estimates due to impact of cyclospora outbreak. Company raises outlook.

Mediterranean fast-casual chain Cava ( CAVA ) posted earnings and revenue that fell short of Wall Street's expectations as the company saw strength to end the quarter, following industry pressure.

Cava revenue came in at $353.7 million, below the $358.7 million the Street expected, per Bloomberg estimates. Adjusted earnings per share came in at $0.11, one penny lower than forecasts. Same-store sales grew by 3.1%, a touch lower than the 3.3% the Street hoped for.

"We saw obviously broader concerns around fresh produce consumption early in the quarter that certainly impacted trend, we saw that bounce back as we worked through the quarter and then toward the end of the quarter," CEO Brett Schulman told Yahoo Finance.

Schulman added, "Post Labor Day, we did see a bit of choppiness around the re-emergence of high gas prices as they spiked, but then saw that abate, things firm up and strengthen as we exited the quarter and have seen that carryover into Q4."

He said that gave the company confidence to raise its outlook for the full fiscal year. It now expects same-store sales to increase between 6% and 7%, up from the previously expected range of 4.5% to 6.5%. The updated forecast is in line with the Street's 6.7% expectation.

The company plans to open 76 to 78 restaurants this year, but the company noted that pre-opening costs did get more expensive, driven by pre-opening labor costs. Its new restaurant design is also resonating with customers, who are seeing an increase in in-restaurant dining, especially at dinner. Schulman said that's not at the expense of digital orders, which account for 38.5% of revenue.

Tue, November 3, 2026 at 9:33 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell

AMD beats Q3 estimates as data center revenue climbs 97%

AMD ( AMD ) reported its third quarter results after the bell on Tuesday, beating expectations on the top and bottom lines, as the company's data center revenue grew 97%.

AMD stock climbed more than 4% following the news.

"Demand for our Instinct and EPYC products continued to strengthen, and we expect growth to accelerate further in the fourth quarter as we scale Helios and 'Venice' production," CEO Lisa Su said in a statement.

"With our leadership product portfolio and deep customer and supply chain relationships, we are confident in our ability to sustain very strong revenue growth and expanding profitability over the coming years."

For the quarter, AMD saw earnings per share (EPS) of $2.09 on revenue of $13.38 billion. Analysts were projecting EPS of $1.97 on revenue of $13.08 billion, according to Bloomberg consensus estimates.

The company saw EPS and revenue of $1.20 and $9.2 billion, respectively, in the same period last year.

Tue, November 3, 2026 at 9:32 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell

Duolingo stock jumps as daily users surge, company raises guidance

Duolingo ( DUOL ) stock jumped 10% after the company reported that its daily active users (DAUs) rose 29% year over year to 64.9 million. Paid subscribers for the language learning platform grew 14% annually to 13.1 million.

But the company is eyeing stronger user growth as it targets a goal of 1 billion users. Duolingo said its operating expenses increased 24% year over year. Those expenses included $11.4 million that the company set aside for a company-wide performance bonus for employees if it achieves DAU growth of 25% or greater in Q4.

Here's what Duolingo reported in Q3, versus estiamtes compiled by S&P Global Market Intelligence:

Revenue: $309 million, up 12% year over year, versus estimates of $303 million

Earnings per share: $0.58, versus estimates of $0.56

Guidance: Raised across all key financial metrics. Revenue is expected at $1.22 billion, ahead of the Street's forecast of $1.20 billion

"We expect to finish 2026 at the high end of both the 10% to 12% bookings growth and 15% to 18% revenue growth targets we set at the start of the year. We expect full-year Adjusted EBITDA of $323 million, or a 26.5% margin, up $3 million from our previous guidance, and $21 million above the midpoint of our original 2026 guidance provided in February," the company stated.

Tue, November 3, 2026 at 9:19 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell

Super Micro tops Q1 estimates, offers strong Q2 outlook

Yahoo Finance's Daniel Howley reports:

Data center infrastructure company Super Micro ( SMCI ) reported its fiscal first quarter earnings after the bell on Tuesday, beating Wall Street's expectations on the top and bottom lines and providing a better-than-anticipated outlook for Q2.

The company said it anticipates Q2 sales of between $19.5 billion and $21.5 billion. Analysts were calling for $16.35 billion.

Super Micro stock rose more than 5% immediately following the news.

"Supermicro's transformation into a Total AI and IT Datacenter Solution provider continues to accelerate, delivering record revenue of $19.9 billion for the first quarter fiscal 2027," CEO Charles Liang said in a statement.

"DCBBS is driving significant value for our customers—from gigawatt-scale datacenters down to single-container PODs—which, including our expanding software, proactive service, and networking solutions, is enhancing profitability and long-term shareholder value. Through key enterprise partnerships and expanding global production capacity, we are making AI infrastructure faster to deploy, superior up-time and more cost-effective for our customer base."

Tue, November 3, 2026 at 5:20 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell

Pfizer focuses on GLP-1, oncology drug development as COVID product sales decline

Pfizer ( PFE ) stock fell slightly on Tuesday despite reporting an earnings beat and upbeat guidance. The pharmaceutical company said it saw operational revenue growth contributions from several treatments, including Eliquis, Paxlovid, the Vyndaqel family, Nurtec, and Lorbrena, during the quarter, though its COVID-19 products declined.

In the earnings call, Pfizer said it expects to spend $10.8 billion-$11.8 billion on research and development this year, particularly on developing its oncology and obesity pipeline. Pfizer is working on berobenatide, a GLP-1 injectable administered only once a month rather than weekly, as well as several cancer drugs.

"Pfizer had another strong quarter with commercial momentum and disciplined execution while advancing our strategy for creating long-term shareholder value," CEO Albert Bourla said in a release. "Our obesity program continued to advance and recent milestones in oncology, immunology and vaccines further demonstrate the potential of our pipeline."

In the third quarter, Pfizer reported revenue was little changed year over year at $16.6 billion, ahead of analyst estimates of $15.9 billion, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence. Earnings per share came in at $0.56, beating Wall Street's estimates of $0.48 per share.

Pfizer lifted its full-year revenue guidance to a range of $62 billion to $64 billion, up from $60.5 billion to $62.5 billion previously. The company also raised and narrowed its 2026 earnings per share guidance to $2.95 to $3.05.

Tue, November 3, 2026 at 4:37 PM UTC Ines Ferré

Shopify stock tanks as Q3 revenue, total order value miss Wall Street estimates

Shopify ( SHOP ) stock plunged 7% on Tuesday after reporting third quarter results that missed the mark on several key metrics.

The cloud-based e-commerce platform's Q3 revenue of $3.74 billion came in just shy of consensus estimates of $3.75 billion for the first time since 2022, according to Bloomberg data. Subscription revenue for the quarter of $836 million also missed Wall Street expectations of $850.2 million, raising concerns about growth in its main recurring-revenue business.

Gross merchandise volume, or the total dollar value of orders sold through Shopify's platform, was $119.15 billion, also falling short of estimates of $120.08 billion.

Shopify's adjusted earnings per share of $0.49 topped estimates of $0.48.

Mon, November 2, 2026 at 9:39 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell

Apple tops Q4 estimates on strong iPhone sales, but misses on China revenue

Apple ( AAPL ) stock is declining in extended trading after beating on earnings but missing on China revenue.

Yahoo Finance's Dan Howley reports on the quarter:

Apple reported its fourth quarter earnings after the bell on Monday, beating expectations on the top and bottom lines on strong iPhone sales.

This is Apple's first earnings call with new CEO John Ternus , who took over the role from Tim Cook on Sept. 1.

For the quarter, Apple reported earnings per share (EPS) of $2.10 on revenue of $114.48 billion. Wall Street was looking for EPS of $2 on revenue of $113.46 billion, according to Bloomberg analyst consensus estimates.

The company saw EPS of $1.85 and revenue of $102.46 billion in the same period last year.

Read live updates and analysis from the quarter and earnings call >

Mon, November 2, 2026 at 9:24 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell

Roku sales grow 24% year over year ahead of Fox acquisition

Roku ( ROKU ) reported a substantial earnings beat on Monday, driven by its ninth straight quarter of double-digit advertising growth.

Here's what Roku reported, compared to Wall Street analyst estimates compiled by S&P Global Market Intelligence:

Revenue : up 24% year over year to $1.5 billion, versus estimates of $1.41 billion.

Advertising revenue grew 23% YoY to $727 million.

Subscriptions revenue grew 23% YoY to $581 million.

Earnings per share: $1.20, versus estimates of $0.55.

Guidance: None given.

Roku stock was little changed following the report.

In June, Roku entered an agreement to be acquired by Fox ( FOX ). The company said that, in light of its pending takeover, it would not host an earnings call or provide a forecast.

"Our third quarter demonstrated that we succeed when our partners succeed, whether it is a streaming service gaining subscribers through Premium Subscriptions, a content company monetizing its library on The Roku Channel, an advertiser buying through a third-party DSP, or a TV brand choosing the Roku TV OS," CEO Anthony Wood wrote in a press release.

Mon, November 2, 2026 at 9:11 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell

Palantir raises full-year revenue outlook as US commercial sales accelerate

Yahoo Finance's Ines Ferré reports:

Palantir ( PLTR ) beat Wall Street estimates on its third quarter revenue and profit on Monday and raised its full-year revenue outlook as the data software company's US commercial business surpassed its US government sales for the first time ever.

Palantir reported Q3 revenue of $2.313 billion, a 96% increase from the previous year. Wall Street had expected revenue of $2.17 billion, according to Bloomberg data.

Palantir now sees full-year revenue between $8.530 billion and $8.534 billion, topping analyst estimates of $8.2 billion. The company also raised its US commercial sales target to more than $3.559 billion. Adjusted earnings per share of $0.44 also beat consensus estimates of $0.40.

news.Title: Marvell Agreed to Pay $1,132 a Share for Lumentum. The Stock Trades Near $510. Here's Why It’s Not as Good As It Looks.
news.Content:
When Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL) agreed to acquire Lumentum (NASDAQ:LITE) on Nov. 2, the deal valued Lumentum at about $1,132 per share, a roughly 24% premium over its pre-talks trading price. Three days later, Lumentum closed at about $510.

That's not quite the bargain it seems. Even based on the current value of Marvell's offer, Lumentum trades at about 85% of what it would be worth if the deal closes, a gap of about 15% (we'll discuss why we say "current value" in a bit). Here's why that gap exists, and why I don't think it's free money.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

The deal's value keeps shrinking

First of all, Marvell is paying for Lumentum entirely in stock. The acquisition price is well over $100 billion (based on Marvell's share price before the announcement), and acquiring Lumentum for cash simply wouldn't be practical. Lumentum shareholders will receive 4.5 Marvell shares for each share they own when the deal closes. There's no collar, a feature some deals use to protect sellers if the buyer's stock falls. So every $1 drop in Marvell's share price cuts $4.50 from the deal's value for Lumentum investors.

Marvell's stock has fallen sharply amid recent market turbulence. It closed at $133.55 on Nov. 5, which puts the offer at about $601 per Lumentum share. That's far less than the $913.95 Lumentum traded for before the deal talks became public. In other words, the premium Lumentum shareholders were promised is gone, at least for now, because it is 100% dependent on Marvell's stock price.

This could take a while

Here's a big reason why there's still a gap, even below the new, lower value of the deal. The companies don't expect to close the deal until the first half of 2028, and the merger agreement allows extensions as late as August 2028 if regulators are still reviewing it. If the deal closes, Lumentum's stock would be worth exactly 4.5 times what Marvell shares are. But spread over that much time, a 15% gain works out to roughly 8% to 13% annualized returns by my estimate, depending on when the deal closes. And the deal closing isn't exactly a sure thing.

Regulators are the biggest wild card. Bank of America downgraded Marvell after the announcement, citing a long review process "that includes China." There's good reason for concern. China's regulator never approved Intel's (NASDAQ:INTC) planned acquisition of Tower Semiconductor (NASDAQ:TSEM), which collapsed in 2023. Even deals that do get approved can take a long time. Synopsys ' (NASDAQ:SNPS) acquisition of Ansys took about 18 months to clear.

Story Continues

If the deal falls apart, Marvell would owe Lumentum a $3.2 billion termination fee. That sounds like a lot, but it works out to roughly $35 per Lumentum share, a small cushion for a stock trading above $500.

What this means for investors

Professional arbitrage investors typically buy the target and short the acquirer's stock to lock in the spread. And in this case, it might seem like a good idea for your portfolio. After all, 15% is quite a gap on an already beaten-down stock. Most individual investors shouldn't be doing that. Without that hedge, buying Lumentum today is largely a bet on Marvell's stock, with regulatory risk layered on top.

To be fair, Lumentum would be fine on its own. Its revenue grew 137% last quarter, and management expects more growth this quarter. In a nutshell, if the deal breaks, the stock wouldn't necessarily collapse.

Having said all that, if I wanted exposure to this deal, I'd rather own Marvell directly than buy Lumentum and hope the spread closes. The gap between Lumentum's price and the offer isn't a mistake. It's the market's price for time, uncertainty, and Marvell's own volatility.

news.Title: 群聯法說會》 最高砸近46億元買庫藏股  執行長：對公司未來有信心
news.Content:
NAND控制晶片大廠群聯（8299）今日召開第三季法人說明會，第三季稅後賺破305億元，一年翻12倍，針對董事會拍板要買回2000張庫藏股，執行長潘健成表示，近期股市雜音多，用行動展現對未來的信心。

台股今（6）日盤中一度崩跌近4,000 點，記憶體控制晶片廠群聯（8299）儘管前三季繳出大賺超過32個股本的亮眼成績單，仍難逃市場賣壓波及；盤中最深一度跌至1,405元的跌停價，隨後跌幅收斂，終場下跌 60 元、以 1,500元作收，跌幅 3.85％。

為提振市場信心，群聯董事會今日也拍板最新庫藏股計畫。預計自今年11月6日至116年1月5日，買回2,000張，買回區間價格為每股 1,680 元至 2,280 元，也就是最高砸近46億元，群聯表示，若公司股價低於區間價格下限，仍將繼續執行買回，此舉主要目的為轉讓股份予員工。

執行長潘健成指出，會買回庫藏股，主要是鑑於近期股市出現不少雜音，希望透過實際的買回行動，向市場與投資人展現對公司未來營運發展的堅定信心。

受惠AI基礎建設及企業級儲存需求強勁，第三季營收860.76億元，年增374.6%，稅後淨利305.48億元，一年翻12倍，每股稅後盈餘（EPS）高達138元，優於前季118.57元及去年同期10.75元。

news.Title: This chip inspection leader fell 24.5% in a month: is the dip worth a look?
news.Content:
Investing.com and Yahoo Finance LLC may earn commission or revenue on some items through the links below.

Investing.com — Semiconductor equipment stocks spent October under heavy pressure, as heightened export restrictions and cyclical pauses in foundry capital expenditures dragged the sector down 25% to 35%. While the broad sell-off swept up lithography and etching leaders like ASML Holding (NASDAQ:ASML) and Lam Research (NASDAQ:LRCX) , it also knocked process diagnostics leader KLA Corporation (NASDAQ:KLAC) down 24.5% over the past month.

Yet treating all equipment suppliers equally ignores a critical manufacturing bottleneck. While chipmakers can temporarily delay purchasing new wafer fabrication tools during cyclical lulls, they cannot bypass the defect inspection and yield management systems KLA provides. As advanced computing shifts toward 2-nanometer nodes and complex 3D packaging, even microscopic wafer defects carry catastrophic financial costs.

Spotting when an essential supplier gets dragged down by a broad sector sell-off is exactly what InvestingPro's ProPicks AI models look for. During the live November 1 rebalance, the system added KLA Corporation to the Tech Titans strategy, pairing it with high-conviction technology leaders—including a specialized foundry chipmaker, an enterprise collaboration software platform, and an essential cloud infrastructure provider.

See the tech picks in the live November update: Explore the Tech Titans strategy on InvestingPro

The inspection step chipmakers cannot skip

KLA supplies the inspection, metrology and data analytics systems that chipmakers such as TSMC and Samsung use to catch defects and manage yield. The Pro Research Report puts its share of semiconductor metrology and inspection at an estimated 50% to 74%, and the switching costs from that integration into customer workflows are high.

Results from the September quarter point to a sector-wide sell-off, with the business itself on firmer ground. Fiscal first-quarter revenue hit a record $4.14 billion, up 29% from a year earlier and ahead of the $4.04 billion analysts expected. Operating margin reached 46.1%, the first time in company history above 46%, on a 62.7% gross margin, and free cash flow was $1.34 billion. Guidance for the December quarter of about $4.7 billion sits well above the roughly $4.49 billion Street estimate.

Backlog reached nearly $13 billion, up about 60% from fiscal 2025, with visibility into 2027 and early 2028. Services revenue added $850 million, up 14%, on a growing installed base. Advanced packaging revenue is on track for about $1.1 billion this calendar year, up more than 70%, and management expects the wafer equipment market to top $200 billion in 2027.

Story Continues

A record quarter set against specific risks

According to consensus analyst projections compiled on InvestingPro, earnings per share are expected to reach $5.46 in fiscal 2027, a 45.3% jump, and $6.65 in fiscal 2028. Over the past 90 days, there have been 19 upward earnings revisions against 3 downward. Citi, Cantor Fitzgerald and Evercore ISI all trimmed price targets after the report, Cantor's to $225 from $325, though each kept a positive rating.

InvestingPro's Financial Health framework, which benchmarks companies across more than 100 indicators, rates KLA "Good," with a Profitability rating of 9 out of 10 and a Piotroski score of 8 behind it.

Memory input costs are a drag of about 100 basis points on gross margin, with relief not expected until mid-to-late 2027 or into 2028. China is set to slip from about 30% of revenue to the low 20s in 2027, supply lead times average about 12 months, and a single weekend of AI-slowdown talk in September knocked 7.8% off the shares in pre-market trading. The stock also still carries a premium earnings multiple.

The KLA Corporation Pro Research Report sets out the process control market share estimates, the 2-nanometer fab transition and whether operating margins can hold.

Looking beyond cyclical equipment sell-offs

KLA's recent operating results highlight the resilience behind its franchise, delivering a record $4.14 billion quarter alongside an elite 46.1% operating margin. When broader sector sell-offs outpace operational reality, valuation discounts emerge in businesses whose products customers simply cannot cut from their budgets.

Capturing those opportunities before broad sentiment normalizes is why ProPicks AI evaluates company fundamentals monthly. Rather than attempting to time macro semiconductor cycles, the Tech Titans strategy systematically rebalances toward proven cash generators with dominant pricing power—spanning semiconductor inspection, chip manufacturing, developer software, and enterprise cloud infrastructure.

news.Title: 〈群聯法說〉Q3每股賺138元創高 擬買回2000張庫藏股「展現對營運的信心」
news.Content:
NAND控制晶片大廠群聯(8299-TW)今(6)日召開法說會並公布第三季財報，稅後純益305.48億元，季增16.5%、年增1,272%，每股純益(EPS)達138元，創歷史新高；累計前三季稅後純益719.37億元，年增1,750%，每股純益325.49元，董事會也通過將買回2,000張庫藏股。

群聯執行長潘健成表示，近期股市雖有一些雜音，但希望透過庫藏股計畫，向市場展現對自身營運的信心。第三季全季維持零負債營運，未向銀行借款，帳上仍有200多億元現金，財務體質穩健。

群聯此次庫藏股預計執行期間為11月6日至2027年1月5日，買回價格區間為每股1,680至2,280元，預計買回總金額上限45.6億元，買回股份將轉讓予員工。

群聯第三季合併營收860.76億元，季增26.8%、年增374.6%；毛利率59.7%，季減5.6個百分點、年增27.3個百分點；營業利益328.98億元，季增24.8%、年增2,210%，營業利益率38.2%，季減0.6個百分點、年增30.4個百分點。其中，研發費用達152.88億元，反映持續投入長期技術與產品布局。

潘健成表示，群聯積極投入先進製程研發、光罩費用、AI儲存及邊緣AI平台開發，並延攬關鍵人才、提升員工獎酬，相關投資有助提高高價值產品比重，強化未來競爭力。此外，也將持續擴充研發團隊，未來半年預計招募最多250名工程師，投入AI網路、AI系統、AI PC及客製化控制器等領域，以因應新產品開發及客戶需求。

news.Title: Nasdaq Suffers Worst AI Panic in Years as Nvidia, SanDisk, and Western Digital Sink
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.5% on Thursday, entering correction territory as concerns about potential restrictions on artificial intelligence infrastructure and post-election policy changes triggered a broad technology selloff.

The decline erased about $2.5 trillion in market value, with investors reassessing the outlook for data center development after Democrats made gains in the U.S. midterm elections. Proposals for temporary data center construction pauses and possible reductions in energy and tax incentives added to concerns about future AI investment.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 6 Warning Signs with TSLA.

Is ^NDX fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

Semiconductor stocks bore much of the selling pressure. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped more than 12%, its steepest daily decline since 2020, while Nvidia ( NASDAQ:NVDA ) slid 9.2%. SanDisk and Western Digital fell 22% and 17%, respectively, as investors reduced exposure to AI-related hardware companies.

The rapid downturn also prompted margin calls and forced selling, contributing to losses across technology shares and other market segments. Hedge funds and retail investors reportedly unwound leveraged positions as the selloff accelerated.

The Nasdaq's move into correction territory followed a sharp reversal in sentiment toward AI-related investments and infrastructure spending.

news.Title: Stock-Split Watch: Is Meta Platforms Next?
news.Content:
Meta Platforms (NASDAQ: META) is officially on board the stock-split train. The artificial intelligence (AI) hyperscaler and social media giant formally announced plans to create a new, nonvoting Class C stock. It will do this via a stock dividend distributed from existing Class A and Class B shares. When the dust settles, the move is effectively a 2-for-1 stock split.

Sorry to ruin the suspense, but yes, Meta is the next big tech company to split its stock . What does that mean for existing shareholders, and does the split make Meta stock a buy now? Here's everything you need to know.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

The ins and outs of Meta's new stock split

Conventional stock splits are similar to slicing a pizza in more ways. The pizza itself remains the same size, but there are more, smaller slices to go around. It works the same for stock splits. The share price and per-share financials fall in proportion to the split ratio.

For instance, suppose you owned a share of company XYZ trading at $100 per share, with earnings per share of $10. Following a 2-for-1 split, you would instead own two shares trading at $50 each, each with earnings per share of $5.

Meta is essentially doing a 2-for-1 stock split by awarding one Class C share to shareholders for each Class A or Class B share they own. The value for Meta here is that this essentially creates a larger pool of stock it can award for stock-based compensation or other purposes, without diluting CEO Mark Zuckerberg's voting control over the company. This will go into effect on Jan. 19, 2027.

Here's the real reason to buy Meta Platforms stock

Remember, stock splits generally don't create value on their own. The pie, or Meta in this case, remains the same size overall. But there are some really good reasons to buy Meta Platforms, or, at the very least, to consider it one of the biggest long-term winners in the AI space.

First, Meta is one of the few AI companies that can internally fund its AI capital expenditures thanks to its massive digital advertising business and social media platforms. Meta is selling bonds to raise capital, but it's a big positive that debt is secondary funding rather than the primary lever.

YCharts.

Additionally, Meta may have found the breakthrough AI product it was searching for with Muse, its consumer AI agent app. Muse is always on and can perform tasks for users, including transactions. It went viral shortly after its launch and remains near the top of app stores.

Story Continues

Given Meta's strong finances and blossoming Muse app, it's hard not to like the company's prospects, split or no split.

news.Title: 前3季每股賺破325元仍還逃跌停！千金股群聯宣布買回2千張庫藏股自救
news.Content:
今年前3季狂賺逾「32個股本」卻仍敵不過大盤股災跌停！群聯（8299）今（6）日重訊公告，為維護股東權益並激勵員工向心力，董事會決議將自今（6）日起至明年1月5日止，大手筆實施庫藏股，預計砸下最高45.6億元買回2,000張股票。

根據群聯公布的最新財務數據，今年前三季（1月至9月）營運表現相當亮眼，累計合併營收達1,949.32億元，營業毛利1,208.39億元，營業利益74.11億元，歸屬於母公司業主淨利達719.38億元，累計基本每股盈餘（EPS）高達 325.49元，相當於前三季就賺進超過32個股本。

不過，今日台股盤中一度大跌近4,000點，身為高價千金股的群聯股價也難逃跌停命運，重訊公告，董事會今日迅速拍板買回庫藏股計畫，預計買回期間自今年11月6日至116年1月5日，預計買回2,000張，佔已發行股份總數0.90%，買回區間價格每股1,680元至2,280元，若公司股價低於區間價格下限，將繼續執行買回，買回目的是轉讓股份予員工。

群聯強調，本次買回股份將用於轉讓給員工以提升向心力，若後續股價因市場波動低於預定價格區間下限，公司仍將持續執行買回，藉此在台股劇烈震盪之際展現基本面強勁的穩健底氣。

news.Title: What Stabilus (STM) Said on Its Q4 Earnings Call
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Stabilus SE? Here are five stocks we like better.

Stabilus lowered its 2030 target to €1.5 billion in revenue and a 12%–15% EBIT margin, from a previous goal of about €2 billion in sales, citing weaker automotive volumes and removing a potential acquisition from its plans.

Preliminary fiscal 2026 revenue fell to €1.197 billion from €1.296 billion, while adjusted EBIT declined to €124 million. The company recorded a €66.7 million goodwill impairment tied to weaker automotive and manufacturing-equipment prospects, particularly in North America.

Stabilus plans to diversify growth toward industrial automation, robotics, and door-actuation systems, while targeting €30 million–€32 million in annual savings from its transformation program. It also plans to propose a €0.22-per-share dividend to preserve funds for debt repayment.

Stabilus (ETR:STM) lowered its 2030 revenue target and reported a roughly €67 million goodwill impairment in its preliminary fiscal 2026 results, citing pressure on automotive production and manufacturing-equipment investment, particularly in North America.

Chief Executive Michael Büchsner said the company now targets €1.5 billion in revenue and an EBIT margin of 12% to 15% in 2030. Its previous target was approximately €2 billion in sales with a margin of up to 15%.

→ Apple's Earnings Beat Comes With a Catch for Investors Heading Into the Holidays

The revision reflects weaker automotive volumes and the removal, for now, of a potential acquisition in 2028 or 2029 from the company's planning, Büchsner said. He added that a stronger-than-expected fourth quarter, driven mainly by industrial business, helped lift the preliminary full-year adjusted EBIT margin to 10.4%.

Revenue and margins decline

Preliminary fiscal 2026 revenue was €1.197 billion, down from €1.296 billion a year earlier. Organic revenue declined 5.7%, while currency effects reduced revenue by 1.6% and the divestment of Fabreeka and Tech Products accounted for a further 0.3% decline, according to Büchsner.

→ Are the Fears Around Alphabet's Search Slowdown Warranted?

Automotive sales faced particular pressure in Asia-Pacific and the Americas. Büchsner said lower production volumes at customers, especially in China and North America, weighed on sales of the company's automotive Powerise products.

Adjusted EBIT fell to €124 million from €142 million, and the adjusted EBIT margin declined from 11%. Büchsner said the fourth-quarter industrial performance helped the company exceed its earlier expectation of a margin around 10%.

Story Continues

→ Palantir's $2.3 Billion Quarter Puts Its Premium Valuation to the Test

Net profit rose 8.3% to €26.2 million, despite the impairment. The figure included a €44.7 million gain from the sale of Fabreeka and Tech Products, offset in part by a €66.7 million goodwill write-down.

Stabilus plans to propose a dividend of €0.22 per share. Büchsner said the proposal is at the lower end of the company's policy of distributing 20% to 40% of net profit, preserving funds to repay debt.

North American equipment weakness drives impairment

Büchsner said the impairment followed a goodwill test incorporating weaker conditions in automotive and automotive manufacturing equipment, particularly in the Americas. Customers, including major North American automakers, have been cautious about investment, he said.

Responding to a question from Berenberg analyst Yasmin Steilen about the DESTACO acquisition, Büchsner said expected synergies were on track and attributed the impairment to lower sales assumptions for automotive-related manufacturing equipment in North America.

He said automotive-related applications currently account for approximately 35% to 40% of automation-equipment sales. Stabilus aims to reduce that share and expand its industrial business as part of its 2030 strategy.

Growth plans and restructuring

The revised 2030 plan assumes a broadly flat automotive market, with potential vehicle-production growth of 1% to 2%, Büchsner said. Stabilus expects door-actuation systems to help it grow faster than that market, with annual sales of €75 million to €100 million in 2030, compared with approximately €25 million to €30 million currently.

On the industrial side, Büchsner said the company expects to grow 2 to 3 percentage points faster than assumed GDP growth of 3% to 3.2%, supported by automation equipment, Industrial Powerise and robotics. He said Stabilus had won its first humanoid-robotics contract and sees that business potentially reaching €20 million to €30 million in the next two to three years.

The company's transformation program generated approximately €17 million to €18 million in savings in fiscal 2026, Büchsner said. He confirmed that annual savings of approximately €30 million to €32 million, expected as the measures take full effect, remain on track and are included in the 2030 targets.

Stabilus plans to publish confirmed results and discuss fiscal 2027 guidance on December 7.

About Stabilus (ETR:STM)

Stabilus SE, together with its subsidiaries, engages in the manufacture and sale of gas springs, dampers, vibration isolation products, and electric tailgate opening and closing equipment in Europe, the Middle East, Africa, North and South America, the Asia-Pacific, and internationally. Its products are used in automotive, navy and railways, commercial vehicles, aerospace, marine and rail, energy and construction, mechanical engineering, industrial machinery and automation, health, recreation, leisure, and furniture industries.

news.Title: 【公告】群聯 2026年10月合併營收315.3億元 年增346.27%
Prediction: November Will Be a Huge Month for Broadcom
news.Content:
Broadcom (NASDAQ: AVGO) hasn't been the best stock to own lately. In June, it hit an all-time high, but it has basically gone straight down from there. It's now down by about 38% from its all-time high, but all that could reverse in November. While Broadcom doesn't have any big events of its own coming this month, there are some others that could drive it higher, like the Anthropic IPO.

Broadcom is a major computing unit supplier to Anthropic, as Anthropic has chosen to deploy a large quantity of Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) that were developed by Broadcom and Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG) (NASDAQ: GOOGL). This could drive heightened awareness around Broadcom's stock, but the reality is that it's a viable investment in its own right and shouldn't need the hype of a new IPO to boost its stock.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Broadcom is a great buy in November, and it's easy to see why if you listen to management.

Broadcom's client list is growing

Broadcom's custom AI chips fill a niche that graphics processing units (GPUs) cannot. GPUs are the industry standard in AI computing because they can be programmed to handle nearly any type of parallel-processing workload. But that type of flexibility costs money.

When a computing unit is designed around a narrow workload, it can be optimized to provide superior performance in that application.

This isn't a new concept. These types of chips, known as application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs), have been around for a while. However, the concept has now made its way to the AI world, and Broadcom has been the primary chip design company to usher it in.

Broadcom's client list is growing. Meta Platforms (NASDAQ: META) now has a custom AI chip in the works, and so does AI lab OpenAI. However, Alphabet has also started to sell more of its TPUs to external customers (rather than solely installing them in its own data centers), and those sales benefit Broadcom as well.

These are all major growth opportunities for Broadcom, and could lead to massive stock returns if management's forecasts pan out.

During Broadcom's latest conference call, CEO Hock Tan discussed the long-term outlook. He noted that its AI semiconductor revenue is expected to rise to $58 billion in 2026, then double to $115 billion in 2027. The company then predicts another doubling to $230 billion in 2028. That's an incredible growth trajectory. To wrap up this projection, Tan noted that Broadcom has secured the supply chain necessary to produce enough computing units to deliver that level of growth.

Story Continues

That should be music to shareholders' ears, as it shows that Broadcom is on top of its game and well positioned for major growth over the next few years. However, the market hasn't taken much heed. None of this forecast growth is currently priced into Broadcom's stock.

Broadcom's stock is priced cheaply

At first glance, you might not think a stock trading at 38 times trailing earnings is cheap, which is fair. However, the trailing P/E ratio doesn't consider future growth at all. Valuing Broadcom stock in relation to the earnings it's expected to have in 2027, it trades at about 10 times earnings.

AVGO P/E Ratio data by YCharts. P/E = price-to-earnings.

That's a very attractive price tag, and if a fair value for Broadcom's stock is about 30 times trailing earnings, that suggests that if the company delivers on its guidance, the stock could easily more than double by the end of 2027. That's a pretty attractive investment proposition, and that doesn't even factor in that Broadcom's AI semiconductor business is expected to double again in 2028.

All this points to Broadcom being an excellent AI stock to own for the next few years. With the stock down around 38% from its all-time high, now is the perfect time to scoop up shares. The market may realize what a great value it is, and buy in November to start prepping for what could be an incredible 2027 for the stock.

news.Title: ePlus Inc (PLUS) (Q2 2027) Earnings Call Highlights: Record $1 Billion in Gross Billings and ...
news.Content: This article first appeared on GuruFocus . Release Date: November 05, 2026 For the complete transcript of the earnings call, please refer to the full earnings call transcript . Positive Points ePlus Inc ( NASDAQ:PLUS ) delivered robust growth with net sales up 9.7% and gross profit up 11.2%, driven largely by organic growth across a diversified customer base. The company achieved record quarterly gross billings exceeding $1 billion, with open orders up nearly $750 million year-over-year, indicating strong future revenue potential. Adjusted EBITDA grew 14.3%, outpacing net sales growth, and operating income rose 15.8%, demonstrating improved operating leverage. ePlus Inc ( NASDAQ:PLUS ) raised its fiscal 2027 guidance, now expecting upper single-digit growth in net sales and gross profit, and low double-digit growth in adjusted EBITDA. The acquisition of Daymark Solutions broadens ePlus Inc ( NASDAQ:PLUS )'s Northeast presence and adds Microsoft Tier 1 CSP certification, enhancing capabilities in regulated industries. Data center and cloud net sales grew 39.2%, fueled by AI-related demand, and managed services revenue increased 11.9%, supporting recurring revenue. The balance sheet remains healthy with $381 million in cash, enabling investments in organic growth, strategic acquisitions, and shareholder returns. Negative Points Professional services revenue declined 11.3% due to project delays among large retail customers and a difficult comparison to the prior year's record quarter. Services gross margin decreased to 32.5% from 34.8%, and professional services margin fell to 35.4% from 38.2%, due to higher third-party costs and lower revenue. Operating expenses increased 9.2%, driven by higher salaries, benefits, and acquisition-related costs, which could pressure margins if growth slows. Supply constraints in high-end compute and networking, particularly memory, are causing delays and price increases, potentially impacting product availability and costs. Other expense of $0.5 million compared to other income of $5.2 million last year, due to lower interest income, foreign exchange losses, and a decrease in fair value of contingent consideration. Cash and cash equivalents decreased sequentially to $380.9 million from $448.9 million, primarily due to a significant inventory build-up for large customer projects. The effective tax rate remains elevated at 27.9%, though down from 29.3%, impacting net earnings growth. Q & A Highlights Warning! GuruFocus has detected 3 Warning Signs with PLUS. Is PLUS fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator. Story Continues Q : What is driving the large increase in open orders, and what was the year-over-year comparison? A : Darren Raguel (COO and President of ePlus Technology) explained that open orders rose about $300 million sequentially and nearly $750 million year-over-year, reaching over $1.8 billion versus roughly $1.1 billion last year. The backlog is concentrated in higher-end networking and data center projects, with overall activity building. Mark Maron (CEO and President) added that accelerating AI adoption, data center infrastructure demand, and cybersecurity emphasis fit squarely within ePlus's strengths in both services and products. Q : What conversion rate assumptions for open orders underpin the raised guidance for the second half versus the first half? A : Darren Raguel (COO and President of ePlus Technology) said the company is starting to see previously built open orders come to fruition, including inventory expected to ship in the second half. While a good portion of open orders will push into fiscal 2028, ePlus expects increasing growth as the year progresses. Q : What is the current state of supply constraints, particularly around memory, and when might relief come? A : Darren Raguel (COO and President of ePlus Technology) noted ongoing issues in high-end compute, especially GPU-related areas, with some delays spilling into high-end networking. However, these constraints are not broadly affecting the market with delays; the bigger impact is price increases rather than supply shortages. Q : How are higher third-party costs in professional and managed services affecting customers and pricing, and can they be passed through? A : Darren Raguel (COO and President of ePlus Technology) said third-party cost increases are built into project pricing and passed through to customers. Elaine Marion (CFO) added that some of the higher third-party cost mix reflects the Bailiwick acquisition, which had a higher proportion of third-party costs in its business. Q : What drove the strong second-quarter growth and profitability improvement? A : Mark Maron (CEO and President) highlighted nearly 10% net sales growth and 11.2% gross profit growth, with adjusted EBITDA growing even faster. Operating income rose 15.8%, reflecting improved operating leverage expected to continue in the second half. Growth was largely organic and spread across a diversified customer base, supported by record gross billings exceeding $1 billion. Q : What is the strategic rationale behind the Daymark Solutions acquisition? A : Mark Maron (CEO and President) said Daymark broadens ePlus's presence in the Northeast market and brings a Microsoft Tier 1 CSP certification with expertise in highly regulated and data-intensive industries. The capabilities are expected to scale across all ePlus markets, complement existing offerings, and create opportunities to deliver integrated solutions to a broader customer base. Q : How is AI demand translating into business opportunities for ePlus? A : Mark Maron (CEO and President) said AI remains an important catalyst for technology investment and a significant long-term growth driver, with demand particularly across data center, agentic AI, and security. Darren Raguel (COO and President of ePlus Technology) added that AI-related customer engagements have increased significantly, ranging from use case validation to purchasing and implementation, contributing to a strong pipeline and open order buildup. Q : What drove the decline in professional services revenue, and what is the outlook? A : Elaine Marion (CFO) said professional services revenue fell 11.3% to $67.8 million due to continued project delays among large retail customers, against a difficult comparison with last year's strongest professional services quarter to date. ePlus remains actively engaged with these customers as they work through their plans. Darren Raguel (COO and President of ePlus Technology) noted continued investment in talent, including Field CTO and Principal Technologist teams, to drive strategic services engagements. Q : What is the updated fiscal 2027 guidance? A : Mark Maron (CEO and President) said that given strong first-half performance, a healthy demand environment, and significant growth in bookings and open orders, ePlus is raising fiscal 2027 guidance to upper single-digit growth in both net sales and gross profit, with adjusted EBITDA expected to grow in the low double-digits, reflecting operating leverage inherent in the business. Q : How is ePlus deploying its strong balance sheet and cash position? A : Elaine Marion (CFO) reported cash and cash equivalents of $380.9 million at quarter end, with capital allocation priorities including organic growth investment, strategic acquisitions, and shareholder returns. ePlus repurchased approximately 148,000 shares in the quarter, bringing first-half repurchases to about 400,000 shares for nearly $34 million, and declared a dividend of $0.27 per share payable December 16, 2026. Q : What drove the increase in inventory during the quarter? A : Elaine Marion (CFO) said inventory rose to $271.4 million from $146 million at June 30, 2026, related to several projects for a large customer expected to ship in the second half of the fiscal year. The cash conversion cycle improved to 36 days from 41 days at the end of the first quarter. Q : How did the product and services segments perform in the quarter? A : Elaine Marion (CFO) reported product segment net sales up 12.8% to $547.1 million, led by data center and cloud, where AI-related demand increased significantly, along with strength in security and collaboration. Managed services revenue grew 11.9% to $53.1 million on data center-related demand, while professional services declined 11.3% to $67.8 million due to project delays. Product gross margin expanded 130 basis points to 25.8%, while services gross margin was 32.5% versus 34.8% a year ago on mix shifts. Q : What recognition did ePlus receive from partners during the quarter? A : Darren Raguel (COO and President of ePlus Technology) said ePlus became the first company in North America to achieve Everpure Ambassador status, was named NetApp North American Flash Partner of the Year, and became a certified services partner in Anthropic's Claude Partner Network. news.Title: What MKS (MKSI) Said on Its Q3 Earnings Call
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in MKS Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.

MKS beat its Q3 2026 guidance: Revenue rose 43% year over year to $1.41 billion, and adjusted EPS more than doubled to $4.18. It forecast Q4 revenue of $1.49 billion and adjusted EPS of $5.00 at the midpoints.

Semiconductor and AI-related demand fueled growth. Semiconductor revenue climbed 54% to $638 million, while electronics and packaging revenue rose 43% to $415 million; AI applications are expected to make up about one-third of that segment's Q4 revenue.

Capacity and profitability are key priorities. MKS is expanding manufacturing to meet strong demand, including chemistry equipment orders booked into 2028, while Q3 adjusted operating margin reached an eight-year-plus high of 27.8%. It generated $243 million in free cash flow and authorized a $500 million share repurchase program.

3 High-Growth Unknowns in Photonics That Are Vital for AI

MKS (NASDAQ:MKSI) reported third-quarter 2026 revenue and adjusted earnings above its guidance as demand for semiconductor equipment and AI-related electronics manufacturing drove growth across its businesses.

Revenue rose 43% from a year earlier to $1.41 billion, while adjusted earnings more than doubled to $4.18 per diluted share. The company projected fourth-quarter revenue of $1.49 billion, plus or minus $40 million, and adjusted earnings of $5 per share, plus or minus 38 cents.

→ Apple's Earnings Beat Comes With a Catch for Investors Heading Into the Holidays

The 3 Favored Machinery Stocks To Buy In August

President and CEO John Lee said customer orders remained strong and visibility had improved. He attributed the growth to investments in semiconductor manufacturing and electronics packaging, including demand tied to artificial intelligence.

Semiconductor Demand and Capacity Plans

Semiconductor revenue increased 54% year over year to $638 million, supported by demand for DRAM and logic applications and increased NAND upgrade activity, Executive Vice President and CFO Ram Mayampurath said. Revenue also rose 15% from the prior quarter.

→ Are the Fears Around Alphabet's Search Slowdown Warranted?

Lee said a leading foundry selected MKS's dissolved gas solutions for advanced logic. The company also won a pulsed DC power application in conductor etch, displacing an incumbent supplier at an existing customer. Lee declined to quantify the win but said he believed it would be significant in the future.

For the fourth quarter, MKS expects semiconductor revenue of $700 million, plus or minus $15 million. Lee said he expects the company to continue growing faster than the wafer fabrication equipment market in 2027, though he did not provide a specific growth forecast for that year.

Story Continues

→ Palantir's $2.3 Billion Quarter Puts Its Premium Valuation to the Test

MKS is preparing its manufacturing operations for a wafer fabrication equipment market approaching $300 billion in 2028, Lee said. Its Malaysia super center is expected to ramp over the coming quarters, and the company also plans capacity expansion in North America and Europe.

Lee said there was little supply-chain constraint reflected in the company's current revenue guidance, although that could change. He also acknowledged that shortages of critical parts made by other suppliers could eventually limit customers' ability to build complete tools and affect MKS shipments.

AI Drives Electronics and Packaging Growth

Electronics and packaging revenue rose 43% year over year to $415 million. Chemistry revenue grew 26% after excluding foreign-exchange effects and palladium pass-through, which MKS said was the strongest growth rate in the business's history.

Lee said chemistry equipment sales increased more than 75% in the third quarter from a year earlier. MKS expects full-year sales of more than $300 million, compared with a historical annual peak of less than $200 million.

Current chemistry equipment capacity is sold out through 2027, with orders booked for delivery well into 2028. MKS is expanding capacity in Guangzhou, China, and expects the project to double its overall capacity when completed, targeted for the third quarter of 2027. Lee said the company would try to accelerate that timeline.

AI-related applications are expected to account for about 25% of total electronics and packaging revenue in 2026, up approximately 180% in dollar terms from the prior year. At the midpoint of fourth-quarter guidance, MKS expects roughly one-third of the segment's revenue to come from AI-related applications.

Lee said the company is beginning to see consumables revenue from equipment shipped several quarters ago. Its proprietary chemistries have an attach rate above 85% to its installed equipment base, he said, and carry gross margins well above the corporate average. Most of the third-quarter chemistry growth, however, came from equipment already in the field rather than recently installed machines.

MKS also reported new orders for rigid printed circuit board laser systems, including for optical modules, with deliveries expected to accelerate in 2027. Lee said industry constraints had created an opportunity for the company to gain share in rigid PCB drilling.

Margins, Cash Flow and Outlook

Third-quarter gross margin was 47.7%, including a 30-basis-point benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds that MKS does not expect to recur in the fourth quarter. Adjusted operating margin rose about 700 basis points year over year to 27.8%, the company's highest quarterly level in more than eight years.

Mayampurath said lower-margin chemistry equipment sales and manufacturing expansion costs were weighing on gross margin, even as higher volumes helped. He expects those headwinds to continue into 2027 but said they could become longer-term tailwinds as consumables revenue grows and new capacity reaches fuller utilization.

The company generated $243 million in free cash flow during the quarter and ended it with $676 million in cash and cash equivalents. Its net leverage ratio fell to 2.4 times trailing 12-month adjusted EBITDA, within its target of 2.5 times.

MKS made a €50 million term loan prepayment during the quarter and another $100 million payment on its dollar term loan after quarter-end, bringing year-to-date prepayments above $450 million. Its board also authorized a $500 million share repurchase program. Mayampurath said organic investment and debt management would remain priorities, while the company would consider buybacks opportunistically.

Specialty industrial revenue rose 27% year over year to $360 million, led by datacom and general industrial demand. MKS expects fourth-quarter revenue in that market to remain at approximately the same level. Lee also noted the company's previously announced agreement to sell its Ophir Optics business to TTM Technologies.

MKS expects to provide more detail on its strategy and margin outlook at its investor day in New York City on Dec. 14.

About MKS (NASDAQ:MKSI)

MKS Instruments, Inc (NASDAQ: MKSI) develops technologies that enable precision control and measurement in manufacturing and research environments. The company provides instruments, components, systems and process-control solutions used to measure and control pressure, flow, vacuum, gas delivery, temperature and other critical production conditions.

Its product portfolio includes vacuum solutions, pressure and flow-control instruments, gas and vapor delivery systems, plasma and reactive-gas technologies, power delivery systems, process-monitoring equipment, analytical instruments and materials-characterization tools.

news.Title: Oracle vs. Alphabet: Which Is the Better AI Cloud Stock to Own for the Next 5 Years?
news.Content:
There's a growing list of technology companies investing heavily in artificial intelligence (AI) cloud computing as demand for compute capacity accelerates. Bank of America estimates that data center infrastructure spending will more than double to $2.1 trillion by 2028.

But not every company that's spending money now on AI cloud computing will have substantial sales and earnings to show for it later.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOGL) (NASDAQ: GOOG) and Oracle (NYSE: ORCL) are two prominent cloud companies ramping up their AI investments right now. Still, while Alphabet's cloud sales are accelerating due to its spending, Oracle's debt is worrying shareholders.

Investors wondering which is the better AI cloud stock to own over the next five years need only look at Google Cloud's third-quarter sales doubling for their answer. Here's why Alphabet is the safer long-term bet.

Alphabet's AI spending is accelerating, but so is revenue

Alphabet stock fell hard recently amid investor concerns about its high capital expenditures, which are expected to reach up to $205 billion this year. The spending has resulted in $9.1 billion in negative free cash flow, worrying many Alphabet shareholders.

But investors seemed to misunderstand two factors: First, $5.1 billion of the negative free cash flow was from a one-time fee to the European Commission, making the decline not as bad as it first appears. The second is that Alphabet's AI spending already appears to be paying off amid rising Google Cloud sales.

Consider that Google Cloud sales more than doubled in the third quarter (which ended Sept. 30) to $30.7 billion. That's an exceptionally high growth rate and shows why the company's capex is rising so quickly.

Rising demand for computing capacity is encouraging Alphabet to ramp up spending, and as expensive as it is, demand appears to continue outpacing capacity. The company said Google Cloud has a $561 billion cloud backlog, which it estimates will convert to sales over the next 24 months.

Negative free cash flow isn't great to see, I'll admit. But the company can always pull back spending once it has enough compute capacity. And when it does, its soaring cloud sales will likely help bring the company's free cash flow back into positive territory -- especially considering that Google Cloud's operating income recently tripled to $11 billion and operating margins have increased to 36%.

Story Continues

Oracle is making a riskier AI bet

Oracle is also investing heavily in data center infrastructure, with management saying that capital expenditures will total up to $95 billion this year. That's up from $55.7 billion in fiscal 2026.

Investors have been skeptical about Oracle's accelerating spending, and they really haven't liked how the company is paying for it by taking on debt. To ease concerns, leadership recently said it would limit its capital raises through fiscal 2030 to an additional $20 billion (on top of an additional $20 billion raised recently).

While that temporarily eased investor fears, they came roaring back just days later when Oracle announced it would raise all of that $20 billion immediately rather than over the next few years. Oracle has about $169 billion in total debt, which has spooked investors and resulted in Oracle's stock falling 50% over the past year.

It may not be all bad news for Oracle investors, though, as management says free cash flow could be $30 billion or more in fiscal 2029 -- a stark contrast to its negative free cash flow of $23.7 billion in fiscal 2026.

If you feel comfortable with some additional risk, Oracle stock could be a good investment as the company's spending slows and free cash flow rebounds over the next couple of years.

But I think Alphabet looks like the better AI cloud stock over the next five years. It's already the third-largest cloud player and is poised to generate significant sales from its massive Google Cloud backlog.

news.Title: What NerdWallet (NRDS) Said on Its Q3 Earnings Call
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in NerdWallet, Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.

Q3 revenue rose 11% to $240 million but missed guidance of $244 million to $260 million, as a $17 million drop in auto insurance revenue offset growth in lending and deposit products. NerdWallet said it does not expect to resolve its auto insurance partnership gap in Q4.

Consumer revenue increased 12% to $215 million, while small- and midsize-business revenue rose 6% to $25 million. Declining organic search traffic, including from AI summaries in Google results, continues to pressure parts of the business.

NerdWallet forecast Q4 revenue of $191 million to $203 million and expects full-year revenue growth, while planning increased investment in AI and vertically integrated businesses. Trailing-12-month adjusted free cash flow rose 51% to $129 million; the company repurchased about $11 million of stock in Q3.

MarketBeat Week in Review – 04/27 - 05/01

NerdWallet (NASDAQ:NRDS) reported third-quarter revenue of $240 million, up 11% from a year earlier but below its guidance range, as a $17 million decline in auto insurance revenue offset growth in several lending and deposit products.

CEO Tim Chen said the company's relatively narrow network of auto insurance carriers limited its ability to monetize traffic as more insurers became competitive in acquiring customers. NerdWallet does not expect to resolve the issue in the fourth quarter.

→ Apple's Earnings Beat Comes With a Catch for Investors Heading Into the Holidays

NerdWallet's Growth Story Looks Strong—But Can It Last?

"We were overly optimistic on partnership timelines," Chen said, adding that the company is working to expand its relationships with insurance carriers and third-party agents.

Consumer Growth Offset by Insurance Decline

Third-quarter revenue fell short of NerdWallet's forecast range of $244 million to $260 million. Consumer revenue rose 12% to $215 million, driven by student loans, personal loans and deposit accounts, CFO John Lee said.

→ Are the Fears Around Alphabet's Search Slowdown Warranted?

NerdWallet Climbs 71% In February On Upbeat Full-Year Guidance

Personal loan revenue benefited from an expanded marketplace serving more borrowers, while deposit account growth reflected increased partner budgets. Those gains were partially offset by the decline in auto insurance revenue.

Small and midsize business revenue rose 6% to $25 million, supported by loan originations and renewals. Lee said organic search traffic continued to pressure other products in that segment.

Story Continues

→ Palantir's $2.3 Billion Quarter Puts Its Premium Valuation to the Test

GAAP operating income was $19 million. Non-GAAP operating income was $30 million, at the low end of guidance, representing a 13% margin. Adjusted EBITDA was $40 million, with a 17% margin.

Beginning in the third quarter, NerdWallet changed its definition of non-GAAP operating income to exclude certain accelerated stock-based compensation. Lee said the change resulted in a $3.9 million add-back in the quarter related to a previous acquisition.

Insurance Partnerships Remain a Priority

Chen said NerdWallet has direct relationships with a few of the top 10 auto insurance carriers. One had been particularly competitive in acquiring customers during 2024 and 2025, but other major carriers have become more aggressive this year, he said.

Building direct carrier relationships can take quarters, even after a company establishes sufficient volume or a market reputation, Chen said. He added that NerdWallet has the volume and is holding discussions, but the timing of new partnerships remains difficult to predict.

"We don't expect to resolve the problem in Q4," Chen said.

Search and AI Strategy

Chen said organic search traffic has declined rapidly over the past three and a half years, though the pace of declines has stabilized somewhat in recent months. Educational content has been severely affected as Google places AI summaries in search results, he said, while product marketplaces have been more insulated because they involve inventory, pricing and eligibility information.

Lee described NerdWallet's business as comprising its declining SEO-led content operation, a growing paid marketing marketplace, vertical integration investments and longer-term AI-related projects. The AI projects are not contributing to revenue today but are affecting operating expenses, he said.

Chen said the company is using AI-assisted development to improve software for its in-house agents and is exploring how licensed agents could support consumers shopping through AI assistants. He cautioned that the potential size of AI-driven traffic is difficult to predict and could vary by product category.

In auto insurance, participation by major carriers could depend on concerns including customer churn and the cost of providing quotes, Chen said.

Outlook and Capital Returns

NerdWallet forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $191 million to $203 million and non-GAAP operating income of $9 million to $15 million. For the full year, it expects non-GAAP operating income of $85 million to $91 million.

The full-year outlook includes a $15 million to $20 million negative impact from investments in vertically integrated brokering and advisory businesses, consistent with the prior quarter's outlook. Lee said NerdWallet plans to increase spending on longer-payback vertical integration and AI projects in 2027, which will weigh on non-GAAP operating income in the near term.

Although planning for 2027 is ongoing, Lee said the company expects full-year revenue growth, while growth in the first quarter will be challenging because of the comparison with the prior year.

NerdWallet generated $129 million in adjusted free cash flow over the trailing 12 months, up 51% year over year. It repurchased approximately $11 million of Class A common stock during the third quarter and had about $57 million remaining under its repurchase authorization as of September 30.

About NerdWallet (NASDAQ:NRDS)

NerdWallet, Inc is a personal finance company that operates a digital platform designed to help consumers make informed financial decisions. Its website and mobile tools provide educational content, personalized recommendations and comparison services across a range of financial products.

The company covers categories including credit cards, banking, personal and student loans, mortgages, insurance, investing and small-business finance. NerdWallet generates revenue primarily through partnerships with financial institutions and other providers when users engage with or apply for recommended products.

Founded in 2009 by Tim Chen and Jacob Gibson, NerdWallet is headquartered in San Francisco and serves consumers primarily in the United States.
