news.Title: Tower Semiconductor Ltd (TSEM) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Highlights: Record Revenue of $526 Million ...
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Revenue: Q3 2026 record revenue of $526 million, up 36% year-over-year from $396 million and 14% quarter-over-quarter from $460 million.

Gross Profit: Record $179 million in Q3 2026, up 92% year-over-year from $93 million.

Operating Profit: $127 million in Q3 2026, 2.5x the operating profit in Q3 2025.

Net Profit: $120 million in Q3 2026, representing a 23% net margin, more than double the $54 million (14% margin) in Q3 2025.

Earnings Per Share: $1.06 basic and $1.05 diluted in Q3 2026, versus $0.48 basic and $0.47 diluted in Q3 2025.

Silicon Photonics Revenue: Approximately $240 million contributed in Q3 2026; Q4 2026 annualized run rate expected to exceed $1.1 billion.

BCD Revenue: About 10% year-over-year growth across 200mm and 300mm platforms; forecasted 20% higher blended prices for 2027 versus 2026.

Q4 2026 Guidance: Mid-range revenue guidance of $600 million; full-year 2026 revenue of $2 billion versus $1.57 billion in 2025.

Balance Sheet: Total assets of $4 billion (including $1.8 billion net fixed assets and $2 billion current assets); record shareholders' equity of $3.2 billion (80% of total assets); current ratio of ~3.7x.

CapEx: $920 million SiPho and SiGe investment plan, ~65% paid to date with remaining 35% expected in Q4 2026 and H1 2027; expected full ROI within one year.

Customer Pre-payments: SiPho customer pre-payments (mostly toward 2027 capacity reservation), including $290 million received in Q1 2026, recorded as operating cash flow.

Utilization: All 200mm fabs at 85%90%; 300mm 12-inch fab fully utilized above the 85% model.

Updated Business Model Targets: $3.6 billion annual revenue, $1.63 billion gross profit (45% margin), $1.38 billion operating profit (38% margin), and $1.2 billion net profit (33% margin).

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 2 Warning Signs with TSEM.

Is TSEM fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

Release Date: November 02, 2026

For the complete transcript of the earnings call, please refer to the full earnings call transcript .

Positive Points

Tower Semiconductor Ltd ( NASDAQ:TSEM ) reported record Q3 2026 revenue of $526 million, up 33% year-over-year, with net profit of $120 million (23% net margin) versus $54 million (14% margin) a year ago.

Silicon Photonics revenue reached approximately $240 million in Q3 2026, and the company expects to double capacity by year-end, targeting a $1.1 billion annualized run rate in Q4 2026 and a $2.8-$2.9 billion SiPho run rate by Q3 2027.

Tower Semiconductor Ltd ( NASDAQ:TSEM ) has secured customer demand commitments through 2029 for both 200mm and 300mm production, providing strong long-term revenue visibility and supporting a $3.6 billion annual revenue target with 45% gross margin and 33% net margin.

The $920 million CapEx investment is progressing ahead of schedule, with 65% already paid, and is expected to achieve full ROI within one year, funded by customer pre-payments and long-term agreements.

Tower Semiconductor Ltd ( NASDAQ:TSEM ) is expanding its served market through advanced technologies like NPO (near-packaged optics), integrated lasers, and 300mm expansion, with prototyping engagements with over 10 top customers and potential to double the optical transceiver market.

Story Continues

Negative Points

Tower Semiconductor Ltd ( NASDAQ:TSEM ) faces increasing competition in Silicon Photonics and Silicon Germanium, with a major competitor ramping capacity, which could pressure market share and pricing despite the company's leadership position.

The company's long-term financial model relies on aggressive assumptions, including all fabs operating at 85% utilization post-expansion, which may be challenging to sustain amid market fluctuations and potential seasonality.

Incremental gross margins are expected to decline from the 62% seen in Q3 2026 to a range of 55-58% as additional depreciation from new tools kicks in, potentially impacting near-term profitability growth.

RF mobile revenue is approaching a trough in the low 50s (as a percentage of total revenue), with a dip during the transition from Fab 7 to Fab 10, and the recovery trajectory remains uncertain despite expected growth in 2027.

The company's expansion plans, including Track-2 in Japan, are subject to execution risks and timing delays, with the full ramp of new capacity not expected until 2029, leaving potential for unforeseen challenges in construction and qualification.

Q & A Highlights

Q : Cody Acree of Benchmark asked CEO Russell Ellwanger to level-set the fiscal 2028 capacity support for SiPho and SiGe now that the $920 million CapEx program is ahead of schedule. A : Ellwanger declined to give an exact revenue target but framed it in capacity multiples: Q3 2026 SiPho revenue was $240 million, and Tower will exit Q4 with 2x the start capacity that drove that revenue, which becomes the run rate in Q2 2027. By Q3 2027, another 1x is added via Fab 7/Arai, tripling Q3 2026 shipments to roughly a $2.85 billion$2.9 billion SiPho run rate before integrated laser revenue, which sits on top of that. He also flagged a likely near-term announcement of further SiPho expansion at two 200-millimeter sites.

Q : Cody Acree asked whether the updated $3.6 billion revenue / $1.2 billion net profit business model may already be too conservative given the capacity math. A : Ellwanger declined to comment on it being conservative, calling it "an aggressive target," but added that Tower "wouldn't be giving a target to the Street that we don't have very, very high confidence that we will meet."

Q : Cody Acree asked CFO Oren Shirazi how sustainable the unusually high ~62% incremental gross margin was, and whether it is a new baseline. A : Shirazi said only about 65% of the $920 million in tools have started depreciating, with more depreciation coming from the remaining tranche and Track-1. He therefore reiterated the long-term model assumption of 55%58% incremental gross profit rather than the 65% seen this quarter.

Q : Vijay Rakesh of Mizuho asked how pricing and contracts are shaping up for newer NPO layouts, given multiple NPO versions, VCSELs and integrated lasers. A : Ellwanger said long-term contracts include pricing targets that set a floor, and that NPO resets the pricing curve higher than pluggables, consistent with a more advanced platform. He noted some competitors discount deeply because they cannot compete technically, and that Tower protects margins by being first to market with customers' next-generation applications.

Q : Vijay Rakesh asked whether NPO demand and backlog are shifting toward 3.2T / 400G-per-lane designs, and whether that is a higher-dollar, more complex SiPho layout. A : Ellwanger answered "yes" to both parts, confirming more 3.2T engagements and a higher-value mix.

Q : Simon Coles of Barclays asked for an update on the 12-inch (300-millimeter) SiPho ramp and how it helps Tower maintain leadership amid competition chatter. A : Ellwanger said 300-millimeter revenue volumes began shipping at extremely high yields, with best-in-class DMUX capability and strong insertion loss performance. Most NPO tape-outs are on 300-millimeter at 16 and 32 lanes. He said 300-millimeter capacity, about 10K in 200-millimeter equivalents in Q1, will triple by Q3 2027 and rise further in 2028, with a very large increase once the new shell is built at the end of 2028.

Q : Sahej Singh of Stifel asked whether the tripling of SiPho capacity by Q3 2027 is all Track-1 or includes remaining capacity from the $920 million program, and how many multiples Track-2 adds. A : Shirazi corrected the math: tripling $240 million gives a $720 million quarterly run rate, or about $2.8 billion annualized, not $960 million. Ellwanger added that Track-2 quadruples Fab 7's roughly 10,000 wafers per month of 300-millimeter capacity to about 40,000, which equates to close to 100,000 wafers in 200-millimeter equivalents given the ~2.25x die-size advantage of 300-millimeter.

Q : Sahej Singh asked about the timing of Track-2, noting Tower takes ownership of Fab 7 on April 1, and whether output could arrive in the second half of 2028. A : Ellwanger said Track-2 will be "well underway" in 2028 with building construction starting that year, and 2029 is when the capacity ramp lands coinciding with capacity contracts now being extended into 2029. He said acceleration by a quarter is a target but 2029 is the confident expectation.

Q : Bastien Faucon-Morin of Susquehanna asked how to think about SiPho and SiGe market share in 2027 given a major competitor's capacity ramp. A : President Marco Racanelli said market share is hard to pinpoint in a fast-growing market with room for multiple players, but Tower was first to ramp high-volume, high-yield 200-millimeter and then 300-millimeter SiPho, which underpins customer confidence to extend LTAs into 2029. Ellwanger added that billions of dollars of LTAs through 2029 reflect customer faith in Tower's execution and multi-generation road map, and that Q4 SiPho revenue is breaking a $1.1 billion annualized run rate.

Q : Bastien Faucon-Morin asked about the RF mobile trajectory into 2027, given tape-out activity and the business approaching a trough. A : Ellwanger said the trajectory is very strong after a dip from re-purposing Fab 7 toward optical and re-qualifying customers at Fab 10. He expects sequential growth with Q2 2027 setting absolute records, and teased an unreleased breakthrough figure of merit with at least one elite customer that opens a new market capability. Racanelli noted Tower focuses on the leading-edge "cream of the crop" segment of RFSOI, where capacity is limited.

Q : Richard Shannon of Craig-Hallum asked about the content uplift from laser integration/attach and what attach rates Tower expects over time. A : Ellwanger said integrated lasers open a new served market with appreciably higher ASPs, backed by strong customer forecasts not yet in the model. The die-to-wafer attach also covers indium phosphide 400G modulators and lithium niobate mod

Release Date: November 04, 2026

Positive Points

Purple Innovation Inc ( NASDAQ:PRPL ) generated positive operating cash flow for the third consecutive quarter, with cash increasing to $28.3 million from $24.3 million at year-end 2025.

Direct-to-consumer trends improved in August and September, with combined net sales up approximately 1% year-over-year, driven by e-commerce growth at Amazon and purple.com.

Amazon significantly outperformed, supported by expanded Prime eligibility, improved fulfillment, inventory availability, and advertising efficiency.

Purple Innovation Inc ( NASDAQ:PRPL ) is launching its fullest product innovation pipeline, including new essentials and hybrid mattress collections representing nearly 90% of unit volume, with strong early retailer feedback.

Showroom expansion continues with 57 locations at quarter-end, plans to reach 60 by year-end, and a target of 9-12 new showrooms in 2027; year-to-date showroom comps are up nearly 2%.

Story Continues

Negative Points

Net revenue declined 19% year-over-year to $96.5 million, driven by significant weakness in wholesale.

Wholesale revenue plunged 31% year-over-year, with regional and independent retailers showing declines in sales velocity, distribution slots, and customers.

Gross margin fell approximately 410 basis points to 43.4% due to lower production leverage and inventory adjustments, pressuring profitability.

Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was lowered to $15-$20 million from the prior $20-$25 million outlook, reflecting continued volume deleverage.

Purple Innovation Inc ( NASDAQ:PRPL ) faces a debt maturity within six months and is still evaluating refinancing options and strategic alternatives, creating uncertainty.

Q & A Highlights

Q : How much of the wholesale weakness was industry-driven versus Purple-specific, and what is being done to fix it? A : CEO Robert Demartini acknowledged accountability on both fronts. The category remains weak (mid-to-high single digits and weakening), but he conceded Purple's product line is "a little tired," particularly with regional and independent wholesalers, as the company focused on other wholesale customers. Purple is accelerating innovation, increasing sales coverage, and improving training and support for these partners.

Q : What are the margin implications of the new product launches, and is there risk of trade-down or cannibalization from lower price points? A : The CEO stated the new line has no lower prices and won't carry further price increases given the June actions. Most of the margin pressure this quarter was cost absorption from lower volumes. The new products carry a similar margin profile to the old ones, but the volume energy they bring is expected to push margins back well north of 45% on a consistent basis.

Q : Is the wholesale pressure something new or an inflection point, or a long-standing issue that needs correcting? A : The CEO said it is not an inflection point but rather the result of focusing wholesale efforts on a couple of large customers over the last three quarters at the expense of regional independents. He also noted the June price increases were higher than he would have liked, and the consumer response in Julyespecially around July 4was "pretty negative." Demand has since returned in DTC, with August and September much stronger than July, though wholesale has been slower to recover.

Q : Are the price increases now complete, or is more pricing still working through the supply chain? A : CFO Robert Lucian said the company believes it is done with price increases while monitoring raw material costs. The mid-June pricing took effect immediately in DTC (showrooms and e-commerce), but it takes time to filter through to wholesale customers, so the full pricing was not reflected in Q3. That flow-through in Q4 is one reason gross margin is expected to improve.

Q : What parameters can be shared on the debt refinancing, given the maturity is roughly six months away? A : The CEO said there are multiple options being evaluated for which are best and attainable, and the company expects much more clarity on the path forward as the quarter unfolds and into the beginning of next year. He also noted the special committee continues to evaluate strategic alternatives and engage with interested parties that could provide Purple with scale and capital.

Q : What drove the third quarter revenue decline, and how did each channel perform? A : CFO Robert Lucian reported Q3 net revenue of $96.5 million, down 19% year over year, driven primarily by wholesale weakness. DTC revenue was $60.9 million (down 9%), with e-commerce at $42.4 million (down 6%) and showrooms at $18.5 million (down 16%). Wholesale revenue was $35.6 million, down 31%, with roughly one quarter of that decline due to accounting changes (about $4 million in reductions of revenue from certain payments to customers and a manufacturer under common control with a customer).

Q : How did DTC trends evolve through the quarter, and what is driving the improvement? A : The CEO said July and the July 4 period were weak as June price increases hit demand harder than anticipated, but business improved meaningfully from mid-August. August and September combined saw DTC net sales up approximately 1% year over year, with e-commerce up 2%, driven by growth at Amazon and Purple.com. Amazon outperformed on improved fulfillment, inventory availability, and advertising efficiency, while Purple.com conversion rates improved significantly year over year.

Q : What is the outlook for showrooms, given the 16% decline this quarter? A : The CEO attributed the decline to the prior-year Rejuvenate delivery shift inflating the comparison base and the June price increase. Looking at Q2 and Q3 together, showrooms were 2% below last year with same-store comps down only 1%, and year-to-date showroom comps are up nearly 2% when neutralizing the shipping change. Purple ended Q3 with 57 showrooms, expects 60 by year-end, and targets 9 to 12 new openings in 2027, with same-store comps expected to turn positive again in Q4.

Q : What is the updated full-year 2026 guidance? A : CFO Robert Lucian maintained full-year revenue guidance of $420 million to $440 million, reflecting a stronger Q4 on an improved marketing plan, normal DTC seasonality, and new product introductions, partially offset by continued wholesale pressure. Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was lowered to $15 million to $20 million from the prior $20 million to $25 million, reflecting continued volume deleverage in manufacturing operations.

Q : How is cash flow and the balance sheet trending? A : The CFO reported cash and equivalents of $28.3 million at September 30, 2026, up from $24.3 million at December 31, 2025. Operating cash flow was positive for the third consecutive quarter and totaled $10.6 million through the first nine months, a $38.7 million improvement over the prior year. Inventories fell 10% to $53.5 million, and the company expects to continue generating cash in Q4, traditionally its strongest cash flow quarter.

Q : What is the status of the new product pipeline and its role in reviving wholesale? A : The CEO said Purple has the fullest innovation pipeline in its history, with new Essentials and Hybrid collections representing almost 90% of mattress unit volume. The new Essentials collection launched on e-commerce in early November with a broader market launch around March, while the new Hybrid line replaces Restore and begins rolling into Purple stores in Q1 and shipping to wholesale in March. Both collections will be showcased at the Las Vegas market in January, with early retailer feedback described as very strong.

Q : What cost actions are underway to offset lower volumes? A : The CEO said Purple is managing plant costs, adjusting labor to match production volume, and carefully managing inventory and working capital. news.Title: nLight (LASR) Beats Q3 Earnings and Revenue Estimates
news.Content:
nLight (LASR) came out with quarterly earnings of $0.16 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $0.06 per share. This compares to earnings of $0.08 per share a year ago. These figures are adjusted for non-recurring items.

This quarterly report represents an earnings surprise of +166.67%. A quarter ago, it was expected that this laser maker would post earnings of $0.14 per share when it actually produced earnings of $0.15, delivering a surprise of +7.14%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has surpassed consensus EPS estimates four times.

nLight, which belongs to the Zacks Electronics - Semiconductors industry, posted revenues of $73.76 million for the quarter ended September 2026, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 8.55%. This compares to year-ago revenues of $66.74 million. The company has topped consensus revenue estimates four times over the last four quarters.

The sustainability of the stock's immediate price movement based on the recently-released numbers and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's commentary on the earnings call.

nLight shares have lost about 12.1% since the beginning of the year versus the S&P 500's gain of 12.3%.

What's Next for nLight?

While nLight has underperformed the market so far this year, the question that comes to investors' minds is: what's next for the stock?

There are no easy answers to this key question, but one reliable measure that can help investors address this is the company's earnings outlook. Not only does this include current consensus earnings expectations for the coming quarter(s), but also how these expectations have changed lately.

Empirical research shows a strong correlation between near-term stock movements and trends in earnings estimate revisions. Investors can track such revisions by themselves or rely on a tried-and-tested rating tool like the Zacks Rank, which has an impressive track record of harnessing the power of earnings estimate revisions.

Ahead of this earnings release, the estimate revisions trend for nLight was mixed. While the magnitude and direction of estimate revisions could change following the company's just-released earnings report, the current status translates into a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) for the stock. So, the shares are expected to perform in line with the market in the near future. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

It will be interesting to see how estimates for the coming quarters and the current fiscal year change in the days ahead. The current consensus EPS estimate is $0.11 on $73.2 million in revenues for the coming quarter and $0.52 on $303.89 million in revenues for the current fiscal year.

Story Continues

Investors should be mindful of the fact that the outlook for the industry can have a material impact on the performance of the stock as well. In terms of the Zacks Industry Rank, Electronics - Semiconductors is currently in the top 30% of the 250 plus Zacks industries. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than 2 to 1.

Another stock from the same industry, Marvell Technology (MRVL), has yet to report results for the quarter ended October 2026.

This chipmaker is expected to post quarterly earnings of $1.10 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of +44.7%. The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has been revised 0.1% higher over the last 30 days to the current level.

Marvell Technology's revenues are expected to be $3.16 billion, up 52.2% from the year-ago quarter.

Release Date: November 05, 2026

Positive Points

Revenue and EPS exceeded the high end of guidance, with operating margins expanding approximately 700 basis points year-over-year.

Semiconductor revenue grew 54% year-over-year, driven by broad-based demand and a major foundry win for dissolved gas solutions.

Electronics & Packaging revenue grew 43% year-over-year, with chemistry equipment sales up more than 75% and AI-related chemistry tracking toward the high end of 15-20% of segment revenue.

Strong order visibility extending into 2028, with customers providing better long-term forecasts and MKS outgrowing WFE.

Balance sheet strength with $1.6 billion liquidity, net leverage down to 2.4x, and a new $500 million share repurchase program authorized.

Negative Points

Gross margin faces near-term headwinds from lower-margin chemistry equipment mix and capacity expansion costs, expected to persist into 2027.

Chemistry equipment capacity is sold out through 2027, constraining revenue growth until the Guangzhou expansion comes online in Q3 2027.

Potential supply chain constraints from third-party suppliers could impact customer tool deliveries and indirectly affect MKS.

Pockets of inflation are emerging, which could pressure costs and pricing negotiations.

Specialty industrial revenue is expected to remain flat in Q4 after strong growth, with automotive production soft.

Q & A Highlights

Q : Can you give more color on the visibility that semiconductor customers are giving you today, and your latest thoughts on MKS' ability to outgrow WFE through 2027? A : CEO John Lee said the company is in constant contact with all semi customers, who are giving much better visibility than in the past, extending into the 2028 timeframe, though those are guidance levels while actual bookings are shorter-dated. He noted MKS has always outperformed WFE during up cycles, and with the current guidance the company will likely grow about 40% year-over-year versus WFE in the mid-30s percent range, a trend he expects to continue in 2027.

Q : With chemistry equipment sold out through 2027 and bookings extending into 2028, how should we frame the cadence of E&P growth next year, and how does the larger consumable base allow chemistry revenue to grow faster than equipment revenue? A : CEO John Lee said chemistry equipment revenue is likely to reach the $300 million range in 2026 versus a historic peak that never exceeded $200 million, achieved without new factories by squeezing capacity from existing sites and supply chain partners. The Guangzhou expansion, targeted for Q3 2027, will double equipment capacity and should let revenue growth accelerate in the second half of 2027. Chemistry revenue typically follows 20 to 30 months after a PO, including 6 to 8 months to build, plus installation, qualification and ramp, and that chemistry revenue is now beginning to appear and should accelerate in 2027.

Q : Can you walk us through the gross margin puts and takes for next year, given mix and capacity headwinds but rising volumes and chemistry? A : CFO Ramakumar Mayampurath said gross margins improved sequentially and year-over-year and the company remains within its stated 4% to 7% plus incremental framework, with two headwindscapacity and capability investments and the fast-growing equipment mixmasking underlying performance in the near term. Those headwinds are expected to become tailwinds longer term as chemistry consumables grow on the newly installed base and new capacity reaches full utilization. He expects margins to stay at current levels near term, with a path to higher gross margins to be detailed at the December Investor Day.

Q : You called out NAND upgrade spending and seem to have raised your outlook on greenfield NAND spending for 2027. What signals are you seeing and how do you expect that to grow over the next couple of years? A : CEO John Lee said the NAND upgrade cycle is in full swing and one of MKS' biggest customers has said it has been pulled in, with related RPO visible. Publicly announced greenfields are coming online in late 2027 to early 2028, with equipment going in somewhat before that, so upgrades should continue for most of the period before greenfields take off in the latter half of 2027 and into 2028. He called NAND equipment building a multiyear tailwind supporting AI infrastructure.

Q : Are you seeing supply chain constraints, and are there share gain opportunities arising from them, particularly in MFCs and rigid PCB drilling where a Japanese competitor is constrained? A : CEO John Lee said reported shortfalls in certain commoditiessome of which MKS also makesrepresent share gain opportunities, and the operations team has been delivering well while expanding factories toward support for $300 billion WFE. He noted the supply chain feat of asking thousands of suppliers to double and double again, with the industry potentially adding $50 billion of WFE in a single year. On MFCs and rigid PCB drilling, he confirmed these are share gain opportunities, noting rigid PCB drilling strength that will accelerate through 2027 partly because MKS is already qualified.

Q : How much of the chemistry growth is coming from legacy installed equipment versus the equipment shipped over the last several quarters? A : CEO John Lee clarified that Q3 chemistry revenue grew about 26% year-over-year organically, and very little of that came from chemistry tied to new equipmentthat contribution is just starting. The vast majority of chemistry growth came from equipment already installed in the field, and he expects the new-equipment chemistry percentage to grow over time, supporting continued strong chemistry growth rates.

He noted MKS has operated in semiconductors for 65 to 75 years and has a long history of reacting quickly to cycle changes, and that CapEx intensity remains low at 3% to 5% even while building both a semi fab and a chemistry equipment fab, keeping financial risk relatively small.

Q : Given visibility out to 2028 and WFE approaching $300 billion, do you expect semi and E&P growth to track similar ranges going forward? A : CEO John Lee said semi growth took a couple of quarters to rev up relative to WFE, with Q3 the quarter MKS began materially exceeding WFE as the supply chain ramped. Q : Are you seeing ASP tailwinds or contemplating price increases in equipment or chemistries given tight conditions and inflation? news.Title: This Could be a Major Problem for Alphabet Investors
news.Content:
Alphabet (GOOG) is spending big on artificial intelligence (AI), and it's likely to spend a lot more. In fact, the Google parent expects to spend between $195 billion and $205 billion on infrastructure and other capital projects in 2026. For 2027, the company also warned that spending will rise significantly.

Bank of America analysts believe that Alphabet's 2027 capital expenditures could surge to about $300 billion. While the firm recently kept a "Buy" rating on Alphabet stock with a $430 price target, analysts are concerned about whether Google's AI and cloud business can pay the bills.

More News from Barchart

Dear Tesla Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 29

Why It's Time to Buy the Pullback in Dell Stock

AWS Is on Fire, But Here's Why Amazon Stock Isn't Ready to Fly

Get exclusive insights with the FREE Barchart Brief newsletter. Subscribe now for quick, incisive midday market analysis you won't find anywhere else.

That concern is easy to understand. Alphabet is putting billions of dollars into the computers, equipment, and data centers needed to run AI. But shareholders want to know when those investments will leave the company with more money.

Alphabet Is Spending More Cash Than It Brings In

Here is the clearest example of why investors are concerned. Alphabet generated operating cash flow of $42.3 billion during the third quarter of fiscal 2026. But it spent $51.4 billion on capital projects. That left the company with free cash flow of about -$9.1 billion in Q3. With that being negative, it's not so attractive to shareholders looking for dividends, buybacks, debt paybacks, or even future investments. Now that spending will increase, there's far less attraction to the stock.

When investors buy shares of a company, they are paying for a piece of that company's future earnings and cash. If Alphabet keeps spending more, there may be less cash left over in the near term. That can make investors less willing to pay a high price for GOOG stock. Plus, we have to remember that building a data center costs money way before it starts serving customers. Alphabet needs those customers to eventually bring in enough business to justify the investment.

There are also ongoing expenses. Servers need electricity. Buildings need maintenance. Equipment eventually needs replacing. In other words, today's purchases can affect reported profits for years. That is why investors want more than promises about the future of AI. They want evidence that the extra spending will produce enough additional income — and right now, they can't get that.

Story Continues

Google Search Is Going Through a Costly Change

How Google makes money from AI searches is another issue. Traditional Google searches often display ads with links. Those ads have helped build Alphabet's business. But that's now an issue with AI, which can help answer user questions directly through longer conversations. Unfortunately, according to Alphabet, AI Mode also earns the company less ad revenue from AI searches, although the firm is working to expand ads in AI programs.

Fortunately, Alphabet's AI investments are helping one major business grow. Google Cloud revenue jumped 103% year-over-year (YOY) to $30.7 billion In Q3. The company said demand for its AI infrastructure and services helped drive that increase.

That gives investors a reason to remain interested. If businesses continue buying Google's cloud and AI services, the new infrastructure could support years of growth. For GOOG stock shareholders, that is the key issue to watch. A bigger AI budget could be worthwhile if Alphabet produces stronger financial results. But if spending keeps climbing faster than the cash coming in, GOOG stock could struggle. Of course, we'll learn more when the company releases Q4 numbers in the new year.

What Do Analysts Say About GOOG Stock?

Overall, Alphabet stock has a consensus "Strong Buy" rating on Wall Street. Of the 53 analysts covering GOOG stock, 45 have a "Strong Buy" rating, three have a "Moderate Buy" rating, and five have a "Hold" rating. The mean target price of $404.21 implies potential upside of 43% from current levels. Meanwhile, the high price target of $515 implies potential upside of roughly 83% from here.

Alphabet's AI spending could pay off over time. But it's understandable that shareholders want more than another promise of future growth. They want to see that the money going out today will eventually leave the business and their investment in better shape. That makes the next few earnings reports especially important. Investors will be watching whether cloud growth and AI advertising bring in enough additional cash to ease the pressure from spending. Alphabet doesn't have to prove that every dollar was well spent overnight. But it does need to give shareholders a clearer reason to be patient.

news.Title: Apple, Alphabet, and Meta: 3 Big Takeaways from Recent Earnings
news.Content:
The Q3 earnings cycle has brought several notable releases from the Magnificent 7 group, with Apple AAPL, Alphabet GOOGL, and Meta Platforms META all posting strong revenue growth and several impressive quarterly records.

Apple Posts Record Results

Apple delivered a strong fiscal Q4 release, with total revenue climbing 12% YoY to a September quarter record of $114.5 billion. Earnings similarly reflected positivity, with EPS of $2.10 growing 14% from the same period last year.

iPhone revenue also reached a September quarter record, with Services revenue reaching a new all-time high. The strong results helped Apple finish its fiscal year with record annual revenue of nearly $479 billion.

Importantly, the company's installed base of active devices also reached another all-time high, providing a favorable backdrop for continued Services growth.

Alphabet Sees Explosive Cloud Growth

Alphabet's latest release was highlighted by explosive Google Cloud results, with segment revenue soaring 103% YoY to $30.7 billion. Demand for AI infrastructure and enterprise AI solutions continues to fuel the growth, with Cloud operating income also climbing significantly to $11.1 billion.

The broader business remained rock-solid as well, with total sales increasing 25% YoY to $127.6 billion. Google Search revenue climbed 12%, with AI-related enhancements helping drive stronger search activity.

The results help reinforce the idea that Alphabet is benefiting from AI across multiple areas of its business, rather than just through its Cloud offerings.

Meta's Advertising Momentum Remains Strong

Meta's core advertising business continues to shine, with total revenue climbing 26% YoY to $64.6 billion. Ad impressions increased 10% from the same period last year, while the average price per ad jumped 14%.

The results reflect continued healthy advertiser demand, with AI-driven improvements to recommendations and advertising efficiency also providing a nice boost. Still, spending remains a major focus, with Meta forecasting $135-$145 billion in capital expenditures for 2026.

Bottom Line

The latest releases from Apple AAPL, Alphabet GOOGL, and Meta Platforms META were largely positive from a growth standing.

AI remains a major driving force behind the results, particularly for Alphabet's Cloud business and Meta's advertising operations. And with Apple continuing to post records across its core offerings, the broader growth picture for these technology giants remains constructive.

news.Title: Stock Market Today, Nov. 5: Amazon Shares Slide as Technology Selloff Erases Early Gains
news.Content:
Amazon.com (NASDAQ:AMZN), a global e-commerce, cloud computing, and logistics platform, closed at $260.21, down 2.19%. Thursday's move reflected early election-related gains that faded as technology selling and higher yields took over. Investors are watching the company's AWS cloud computing division's profitability and AI infrastructure spending next.

Trading volume reached 83.5 million shares, coming in about 117% above its three-month average of 38.5 million shares. Amazon.com IPO'd in 1997 and has grown 265,645% since going public.

How the markets moved today

The S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) closed at 7,354, down 4.36%, while the Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX:^IXIC) closed at 24,315, down 5.52%. Among e-commerce, digital advertising, and retail logistics peers, Walmart closed at $127.72, down 1.12%, while Costco Wholesale closed at $1,065.59, up 1.83%.

What this means for investors

On Thursday, Nov. 5, Amazon shares gained during early trading after the company announced a partnership with Uber that provides its Prime members with free restaurant-delivery benefits through Uber Eats. However, that didn't last, as a broad sell-off of tech stocks took place today in the wake of U.S. midterm election results.

The Democratic Party gained control of Congress, raising worries that incoming Democratic leadership could demand tighter AI regulations and put a hold on data center construction projects key to the artificial intelligence (AI) boom. This could result in a major impact to Amazon's AWS business just as the company is spending substantial sums to expand its AI infrastructure.

At the same time, Wall Street is concerned about the e-commerce giant's AI costs. Last week, Amazon's third-quarter earnings report missed revenue estimates while the company's capital expenditures continued to rise, resulting in negative Q3 free cash flow (FCF) of $42.4 billion compared to positive FCF of $14.8 billion in the previous year.

In a macroeconomic environment of rising interest rates, which makes borrowing to fund an AI buildout more expensive, and persistent inflation likely to impact consumer spending and Amazon's sales, the company is facing a challenging time right now. But over the long run, its AI investments could position it for success. Management forecasted AWS revenue to grow by 40% year over year in 2027 and 2028 as well, thanks to strong demand for its AI offerings.

news.Title: Docusign vs. Monday.com: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
news.Content:
Deciding between an established market leader and a high-growth challenger is a common challenge for investors. Today, we compare whether Docusign Inc. (NASDAQ:DOCU) or Monday.com (NASDAQ:MNDY) is the better long-term choice.

Docusign pioneered the e-signature category and now seeks to automate the entire contract lifecycle for businesses of all sizes. Meanwhile, Monday.com provides a highly customizable work management platform that helps teams streamline complex workflows. Both companies compete for enterprise budget in the software space, though they currently occupy very different stages of business maturity.

The case for Docusign

Docusign provides Intelligent Agreement Management, including its eSignature and contract lifecycle management solutions. The company operates in the broader tech stocks landscape, serving over 1.8 million customers globally through various digital tools. Major strategic technology partners include Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ:MSFT), Salesforce.com Inc. (NYSE:CRM), SAP SE (NYSE:SAP), ServiceNow Inc. (NYSE:NOW), Workday Inc. (NASDAQ:WDAY), and Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ:GOOG).

According to its latest annual report, filed for the fiscal year ended Jan. 31, 2026, revenue reached $3.2 billion. This represents an 8.2% increase compared with the prior fiscal year, showing steady expansion in its core markets. Net income for the period was $309.1 million, resulting in a net margin of 9.6% for the latest fiscal year.

As of its January 2026 balance sheet, the current ratio is 0.7x and the debt-to-equity ratio is 0.1x, which measure short-term liquidity and total debt levels. Free cash flow for the fiscal year ended Jan. 31, 2026, reached $1.1 billion. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 53.4% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

The case for Monday.com

Monday.com offers an AI work platform designed to manage and automate work across CRM, service, and development segments. The platform is currently used by approximately 250,000 customers worldwide who utilize its flexible Work OS to build custom applications. By focusing on a no-code interface, the company targets a wide range of departments that need to consolidate disparate work processes.

According to its latest annual report, filed for the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, revenue reached $1.2 billion. This marked a significant increase of 26.7% compared with the prior fiscal year. Net income for the period was $118.7 million, while the net margin improved to 9.6% as the company scaled its operations.

Story Continues

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the current ratio is 2.5x, and the debt-to-equity ratio is 0.3x, tracking liquidity and total debt relative to shareholder equity. Free cash flow for the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, reached $309.9 million. Note that stock-based compensation (SBC for short) represented roughly 53% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

Risk profile comparison

Docusign faces significant revenue concentration, as it relies on its eSignature product for the majority of its total sales. Rapid advances in artificial intelligence could lead to increased competition from general-purpose providers or disrupt the core agreement market. The company also depends on third-party cloud infrastructure from Microsoft and partner platforms to deliver its various services to users.

Monday.com faces intense competition in the productivity and collaboration market from established giants like Microsoft and Adobe Systems Inc. (NASDAQ:ADBE). It must also compete with specialized players like Atlassian Corp. (NASDAQ:TEAM), Asana Inc (NYSE:ASAN), and Smartsheet for limited enterprise software budgets. The future success of the company depends on its ability to maintain high growth rates while successfully cross-selling its newer customer relationship management (CRM) and service products.

Valuation comparison

Based on current Forward P/E and P/S ratio metrics, Monday.com appears more attractively priced relative to its growth profile. The P/S ratio measures market capitalization against sales over the past twelve months.

Metric

Valuation metrics include those sourced from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from those of other data providers.

Which stock would I buy for 2027?

Monday.com is undergoing a bit of a reset. In July, it fired 20% of its workforce. It's part of an effort to redirect more capital to AI services for its platform.

In its second quarter, revenue grew 22% year-over-year to nearly $365 million, but net income was $3.64 million, representing a net profit margin of barely 1%.

Still, there were some bright spots. Management touted a record net addition of $100,000-plus and $500,000-plus (client spending) customers, saying they reflect the continued strength of Monday.com's push to go upmarket. In July, the business crossed $1.5 billion in annual recurring revenue (ARR), a milestone the company says reflects the durability of its core business even as it reshapes the company around AI.

For the full year, sales should rise nearly 20% to $1.47 billion, but net income should weaken to about $68 million.

For Docusign, sales in its current fiscal year are seen growing by nearly 9% to $3.5 billion, with a slightly better percentage gain in net income to $346 million.

Docusign's launch and global expansion of the IAM platform with the introduction of AI-powered tools should position the company for future growth. However, the not-so-great projected revenue growth rates suggest that Docusign may be entering a phase of more mature growth and a landscape of increasingly competitive digital agreement and contract management software. In particular, news reports OpenAI would launch a ChatGPT product that would compete head-on with Docusign in the document summary field caused some investor fears. Right now, however, the signature and identity verification part of Docusign's business appears unthreatened by ChatGPT.

The choice here is to go with the faster-growing business, sales-wise. In the long term, sales growth is the basis on which businesses can generate profits for investors, so given the two stocks' roughly comparable valuation ratios, Monday.com is the choice.

news.Title: Marc Chaikin Sees Alphabet (GOOGL) as a Conglomerate Hiding Three World-Class Businesses
news.Content:
We just published a list of the 10 Stocks That Could Skyrocket in 2027 and Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL) ranked 6th on this list.

Yahoo Finance reported on October 21 that SpaceX opened with its biggest jump since the debut, after third-quarter revenue and profit beat Wall Street estimates. The company's AI business now brings in nearly half of its sales.

A Tesla Tie-Up Could Reshape Musk's Orbit

Gene Munster of Deepwater Asset Management puts the odds of a deal within two years at 95%. A merged company would be worth about $3.5 trillion.

Starlink drives the numbers. Connectivity revenue rose 69% to $5.2 billion, and President Gwynne Shotwell said the service added 1.6 million subscribers in the quarter. There were also 275 hedge fund holders of the stock as of Q2 2026, making it a very popular stock among the funds we track.

A stock the size of Alphabet is an unlikely target for a promoter, but Marc Chaikin built a 100X starburst pitch around it. The creator of the Power Gauge Report calls it his single highest-conviction pick for the age of frontier AI, a candidate for a historic starburst, and says it could unlock far more value than DowDuPont and GE combined did.

Chaikin argues the company is a conglomerate hiding three world-class businesses inside one stock. YouTube already has a streaming service that eclipses Netflix, he says, Waymo runs circles around Tesla in autonomous driving, and Google Cloud is growing faster than Amazon Web Services.

It is the final buy on Chaikin's frontier AI hotlist, and he describes it as the best investment anyone can make right now. news.Title: Earnings live updates: Airbnb stock jumps as Wall Street cheers 'growth mode,' upbeat outlook
news.Content:
The third quarter earnings season is over halfway done, and the reports continue to pour in. This week brought another shot of major earnings courtesy of Apple ( AAPL ), Palantir ( PLTR ), and AMD ( AMD ).

In addition to those tech heavyweights, investors are watching the results out of Roku ( ROKU ), Arm Holdings ( ARM ), McDonald's ( MCD ), QUALCOMM ( QCOM ), Novo Nordisk ( NVO ), Uber Technologies ( UBER ), Toyota Motor Corporation ( TM ), ConocoPhillips ( COP ), and Moderna ( MRNA ).

S&P 500 corporations continue to demonstrate robust earnings growth. According to FactSet data , approximately 60% of S&P 500 companies have already reported Q3 earnings, with an overall earnings growth rate of 30.2%. If that rate holds, it will mark the third straight quarter of earnings growth above 25% for the index.

LIVE 13 updates

Featured

Thu, November 5, 2026 at 10:06 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell

Airbnb 'back in growth mode,' CEO says after strong quarter. Stock jumps after hours.

Airbnb ( ABNB ) stock jumped 11% after hours after the peer-to-peer home rental company touted strong growth across its business and raised its full-year outlook amid healthy global travel demand.

"Airbnb is back in growth mode," CEO Brian Chesky said in a release to investors. "It's rare for a marketplace of our size to reaccelerate growth, but that's exactly what we're doing. In Q3, we delivered our fastest revenue growth in more than three years, with acceleration across our business, including our most established markets."

In the third quarter, Airbnb reported earnings per share of $3.16, surpassing Wall Street analyst estimates of $2.85 per share, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence data. Revenue grew 19% to $4.87 billion, also beating estimates of $4.74 billion.

"In North America, nights booked grew at their fastest pace in four years," the company said. "We're also seeing more guests return to Airbnb, and more people try it for the first time."

The strength of the company's quarter led it to raise its guidance for the remainder of the year.

In the fourth quarter, Airbnb expects revenue to grow 16%-19% to a range of $3.22 billion to $3.28 billion, exceeding the Street's midpoint estimate of $3.16 billion.

For the full year, Airbnb forecasts revenue growth in the high teens and adjusted EBITDA margins to increase to approximately 36%.

Thu, November 5, 2026 at 10:09 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell

Atlassian tumbles 16% on weaker subscription growth outlook

Investing.com reports:

Atlassian Corporation shares plunged 16% despite the company reporting first-quarter results that topped analyst expectations, as its subscription growth outlook disappointed investors.

The collaboration software provider reported adjusted earnings per share of $1.65, beating analyst estimates of $1.43 by $0.22. Revenue rose 24% year-over-year to $1.77 billion from $1.43 billion a year earlier, surpassing the consensus estimate of $1.71 billion. Adjusted operating margin also came in ahead of expectations at 32%, compared with the estimated 28.6%.

However, investors focused on signs of slowing subscription growth. Atlassian forecast subscription annual recurring revenue (ARR) growth of approximately 18.5% year-over-year for fiscal 2027, down from the 23% growth reported in the first quarter.

Thu, November 5, 2026 at 9:52 PM UTC Brooke DiPalma

Bob's Furniture stock rises after better-than-expected results: 'Value is always in vogue'

Bob's Furniture ( BOBS ) reported better-than-expected third quarter results. Revenue came in at $680 million, higher than the $666 million estimates, per Bloomberg consensus data. Adjusted earnings per share also beat estimates by $0.02, coming in at $0.28.

The results were largely driven by customers leaning into higher-cost furniture, with CEO Bill Barton telling Yahoo Finance, "Value is always in vogue."

"The industry continues to struggle, although we think ... the furniture industry stabilized a bit in the third quarter. We're not really calling for a turn yet, ... [but] the trend that we saw in the spring of our customers trading up into the premium price tiers continued in the third quarter. So we saw that average order value going up, and that's really what carried a lot of the comp growth for the third quarter," Barton said.

The company reaffirmed its 2026 guidance, with expectations for same-store sales to grow in the range of 1.5% to 2.5%, but it didn't update its guidance, with Barton calling it a "very dynamic backdrop."

Wed, November 4, 2026 at 9:23 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell

Qualcomm ( QCOM ) reported fourth quarter earnings after the bell Wednesday, topping expectations on the top and bottom lines and providing a better-than-anticipated Q1 revenue outlook.

EPS, though, is set to come in between $2.15 and $2.35 with a midpoint of $2.25. Analysts were looking for $2.32

Wed, November 4, 2026 at 9:18 PM UTC Brooke DiPalma

Mediterranean fast-casual chain Cava ( CAVA ) posted earnings and revenue that fell short of Wall Street's expectations as the company saw strength to end the quarter, following industry pressure.

Cava revenue came in at $353.7 million, below the $358.7 million the Street expected, per Bloomberg estimates. Adjusted earnings per share came in at $0.11, one penny lower than forecasts. Same-store sales grew by 3.1%, a touch lower than the 3.3% the Street hoped for.

"We saw obviously broader concerns around fresh produce consumption early in the quarter that certainly impacted trend, we saw that bounce back as we worked through the quarter and then toward the end of the quarter," CEO Brett Schulman told Yahoo Finance.

Schulman added, "Post Labor Day, we did see a bit of choppiness around the re-emergence of high gas prices as they spiked, but then saw that abate, things firm up and strengthen as we exited the quarter and have seen that carryover into Q4."

He said that gave the company confidence to raise its outlook for the full fiscal year. It now expects same-store sales to increase between 6% and 7%, up from the previously expected range of 4.5% to 6.5%. The updated forecast is in line with the Street's 6.7% expectation.

The company plans to open 76 to 78 restaurants this year, but the company noted that pre-opening costs did get more expensive, driven by pre-opening labor costs. Its new restaurant design is also resonating with customers, who are seeing an increase in in-restaurant dining, especially at dinner. Schulman said that's not at the expense of digital orders, which account for 38.5% of revenue.

AMD stock climbed more than 4% following the news.

"Demand for our Instinct and EPYC products continued to strengthen, and we expect growth to accelerate further in the fourth quarter as we scale Helios and 'Venice' production," CEO Lisa Su said in a statement.

But the company is eyeing stronger user growth as it targets a goal of 1 billion users. Duolingo said its operating expenses increased 24% year over year. Tue, November 3, 2026 at 9:19 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell

Super Micro tops Q1 estimates, offers strong Q2 outlook

Yahoo Finance's Daniel Howley reports:

Data center infrastructure company Super Micro ( SMCI ) reported its fiscal first quarter earnings after the bell on Tuesday, beating Wall Street's expectations on the top and bottom lines and providing a better-than-anticipated outlook for Q2.

The company said it anticipates Q2 sales of between $19.5 billion and $21.5 billion. Analysts were calling for $16.35 billion.

Super Micro stock rose more than 5% immediately following the news.

"Supermicro's transformation into a Total AI and IT Datacenter Solution provider continues to accelerate, delivering record revenue of $19.9 billion for the first quarter fiscal 2027," CEO Charles Liang said in a statement.

"DCBBS is driving significant value for our customers—from gigawatt-scale datacenters down to single-container PODs—which, including our expanding software, proactive service, and networking solutions, is enhancing profitability and long-term shareholder value. Through key enterprise partnerships and expanding global production capacity, we are making AI infrastructure faster to deploy, superior up-time and more cost-effective for our customer base."

Tue, November 3, 2026 at 5:20 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell

Pfizer focuses on GLP-1, oncology drug development as COVID product sales decline

Pfizer ( PFE ) stock fell slightly on Tuesday despite reporting an earnings beat and upbeat guidance. The pharmaceutical company said it saw operational revenue growth contributions from several treatments, including Eliquis, Paxlovid, the Vyndaqel family, Nurtec, and Lorbrena, during the quarter, though its COVID-19 products declined.

In the earnings call, Pfizer said it expects to spend $10.8 billion-$11.8 billion on research and development this year, particularly on developing its oncology and obesity pipeline. Pfizer is working on berobenatide, a GLP-1 injectable administered only once a month rather than weekly, as well as several cancer drugs.

"Pfizer had another strong quarter with commercial momentum and disciplined execution while advancing our strategy for creating long-term shareholder value," CEO Albert Bourla said in a release. "Our obesity program continued to advance and recent milestones in oncology, immunology and vaccines further demonstrate the potential of our pipeline."

In the third quarter, Pfizer reported revenue was little changed year over year at $16.6 billion, ahead of analyst estimates of $15.9 billion, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence. Earnings per share came in at $0.56, beating Wall Street's estimates of $0.48 per share.

Pfizer lifted its full-year revenue guidance to a range of $62 billion to $64 billion, up from $60.5 billion to $62.5 billion previously. The company also raised and narrowed its 2026 earnings per share guidance to $2.95 to $3.05.

Tue, November 3, 2026 at 4:37 PM UTC Ines Ferré

news.Title: Nvidia has lost nearly $1.4 trillion since its October record
news.Content:
Nvidia ( NVDA ) is on track for its fifth straight losing week, and the slide since its October record has now erased nearly $1.4 trillion in market value.

Thursday did a lot of the damage . Nvidia closed down more than 9%, knocking nearly $450 billion off its market value in a single session and leaving the company worth about $4.4 trillion. It was the stock's worst day since the DeepSeek sell-off in January 2025.

Nvidia has plenty of company.

AMD ( AMD ), Micron ( MU ), and Arm ( ARM ) suffered steep double-digit losses, and Broadcom ( AVGO ) and Taiwan Semiconductor ( TSM ) fell more than 10%. The PHLX Semiconductor Index ( ^SOX ) had its worst day since March 2020 and is now more than a third below its June record. Sandisk ( SNDK ) dropped 22%.

Nvidia itself is now about 24% below its Oct. 6 record close and trading below its 200-day moving average .

The trigger this time is Washington. Democrats won both chambers of Congress, and candidates in both parties campaigned against AI data centers , the buildings that run on Nvidia's chips. The Senate came close to passing a bill this fall that would have made data centers pay more of the power costs they create.

Losing streaks this long don't come often for Nvidia. Since its 1999 IPO, the stock has strung together five or more down weeks just 12 times before this one. The longest ran seven weeks, in the summer of 2008.

The last one is the streak bulls will want to remember. It ended in October 2022, about a month before ChatGPT's launch set off the AI boom, and Nvidia's stock roughly quadrupled over the following year.

That's the best case, not the base case. Nvidia was higher 13 weeks later in only five of the 12 earlier streaks, though it was up a year later in eight. The worst came in 2002, when the stock lost nearly two-thirds of its value over the following year.

For now, Washington is the new worry hanging over the stock.

"There will be congressional hearings," Stifel's Brian Gardner told Reuters ahead of the vote. "There will be investigations."

news.Title: Nasdaq Stock Market Correction: History Says This Is What Happens Next
news.Content:
It's been a rough few weeks for tech stocks, to put it mildly. On Nov. 5, the Nasdaq Composite closed about 12% below its record set on Oct. 6, officially putting the tech-heavy benchmark in correction territory for the third time this year.

The correction has had several causes. Some have been earnings-driven. For example, investors have started to question how much more Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) and Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL)(NASDAQ:GOOG) can spend on AI after both missed earnings estimates, and Intel 's (NASDAQ:INTC) stock collapsed about 30% in a single day after weak guidance. Plus, the recent election results have caused investors to fear that the AI infrastructure build-out will be forced to slow down, as several high-profile elected officials are calling for data center construction moratoriums.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Of course, nobody knows what the market will do next. But history can tell us what has usually happened after corrections like this one.

Image source: Getty Images.

Corrections are more common than you might think

A correction is generally defined as a decline of at least 10% from a recent high, and the Nasdaq has experienced a lot of them. According to a Reuters analysis of LSEG data, the Nasdaq Composite entered a correction after a new high 24 times in 44 years, or about once every 1.8 years. This year has been especially choppy. The Composite was in correction territory in March and again in July, and it went on to set new records both times.

The short term is unpredictable. The longer term has been better.

In the month after the Nasdaq Composite first closes 10% below its high, its average return has been slightly negative, according to Schaeffer's Research, which analyzed data dating back to 1971. But six months out, the index has averaged a 13.6% gain and has been higher 73% of the time, more than double its typical six-month return.

The one-year picture is even more encouraging. After the dozen Nasdaq corrections since 2011, the index has gained an average of 22% over the following 12 months, and has been higher in 11 of the 12 cases.

Of course, some corrections get worse

Notice the "11 of the 12 cases" in that last sentence. That one exception is a good reminder that corrections don't always stay corrections. Investors who bought the January 2022 correction were down another 24% a year later, as the decline turned into a full-blown bear market. According to Dow Jones Market Data, about 37% of Nasdaq corrections since 1971 have become bear markets, defined as declines of 20% or more from the previous high. Source

Story Continues

We've seen several of those in recent years, including 2018, the COVID-19 crash in 2020, the 2022 bear market, and last year's tariff-driven sell-off, when the Nasdaq fell about 24% from its December 2024 high. Even then, the index set a new record by late June 2025.

What I'd do now

In short, history suggests corrections have usually been better times to buy than to sell, but it doesn't promise the bottom is in. Nobody can reliably predict where the market or any specific stock will stop declining and reach an inflection point.

Here's a fun fact. The Nasdaq Composite has turned $100 into roughly $25,700 since 1971, averaging about 10.5% per year in gains before dividends, despite dozens of corrections along the way. And trying to time your exit can be costly. Hartford Funds found that missing just the 10 best days in the S&P 500 over the past 30 years would have cut an investor's returns roughly in half, and most of the best days came during bear markets or shortly after.

With all that in mind, I'm not selling anything in this volatile market. If you need money from your portfolio in the next few years, this is a good reminder that it shouldn't be in volatile tech stocks or the stock market in general. But for long-term money, I'm sticking to my plan and using the pullback to add to a few beaten-down stocks I own and buying a few that have been on my watch list.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger

Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005.

But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout, a massive technology build-out that Google's CEO says could be more profound than fire or electricity.

While everyone watches the chip designers, one "backbone" company provides the critical technology that Nvidia and AMD literally cannot function without. We've detailed this under-the-radar player in our new AI Playbook.

Continue »

Matt Frankel, CFP® has positions in Amazon. The Motley Fool has positions in and recommends Alphabet, Amazon, and Intel. The Motley Fool has a disclosure policy .
