news.Title: Stock Market Today, Nov. 3: Marvell Shares Edge Higher After Premarket Drop on $115 Billion Lumentum Deal
news.Content:
Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL), a data infrastructure semiconductor provider, closed at $171.97, up 0.33%. Shares were volatile after a premarket sell-off tied to the company's $115-billion acquisition of Lumentum and several analyst downgrades.

Trading volume reached 37.6 million shares, coming in about 67% above its three-month average of 22.6 million shares. Marvell Technology IPO'd in 2000 and has grown 1,114% since going public.

How the markets moved today

The S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) rose 0.36% to 7,569, and the Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX:^IXIC) gained 0.83% to 25,372. Among semiconductor equipment and integrated circuits for data center and networking infrastructure peers, Broadcom closed at $332.13, up 3.07%, while Arista Networks finished at $169.91, up 3.52%, as AI-infrastructure spending remained in focus.

What this means for investors

On Tuesday, Nov. 3, Marvell shares gained the day after plunging about 13% on its announcement of a $115 billion all-stock acquisition of Lumentum, a provider of optical components critical to efficient data transmission, a desirable feature for artificial intelligence systems. The risk of share dilution from the deal combined with Toronto-Dominion Bank 's TD Cowen issuing a Hold downgrade, contributed to Marvell's stock decline.

The fact that Marvell shares experienced an uptick today signals that Wall Street may have considered the stock oversold. After all, Marvell's move to own Lumentum is poised to turbocharge revenue growth.

Before the deal, Marvell had already raised its revenue outlook for its 2028 fiscal year (FY), ended Jan. 31, 2028, to $20 billion, and set a FY2031 target of $70 billion to $90 billion in sales. This represents massive growth from its FY2026 revenue of $8.2 billion.

Lumentum adds another fast-growing business to Marvell's offerings. Lumentum announced fiscal Q1 earnings on Nov. 2, reporting a spectacular 137% year-over-year increase in sales to $1.3 billion. It's no wonder Wall Street is reassessing the acquisition today.

news.Title: Elon Musk’s Tesla and SpaceX protest NYSE parent's new plan
news.Content:
Elon Musk 's SpaceX (Nasdaq: SPCX) and Tesla (Nasdaq: TSLA), along with Amazon (Nasdaq: AMZN), Netflix (Nasdaq: NTFX), Lam Research (Nasdaq: LRCX), and SoFi Technologies (Nasdaq: SOFI), have finally objected to the tokenization of their stocks on the OKXICE TSV .

OKXICE TSV is a proposed tokenized stock trading platform created by OKXICE, a 50-50 joint venture between the New York Stock Exchange parent company Intercontinental Exchange (NYSE: ICE) and the OKX crypto exchange.

What's behind the objection

Tokenization is the process of using blockchain technology to turn real‑world assets (RWAs) such as stocks, real estate, government bonds, etc. into digital tokens, which can be traded fractionally, 24/7.

While the stock tokens offer traders from outside the U.S. indirect exposure to the American stock market, they don't offer shareholder rights such as ownership, voting, etc., like original stocks do.

It's the Securities and Exchange Commission's (SEC) innovation exemption issued in September that allows exchanges like OKXICE to offer tokenized U.S. stocks without registering as exchanges.

But the exemption also allows companies to object to their stocks being tokenized by third parties like OKXICE.

The platform's initial notice got published on Oct. 4, and the SEC's rule lets notified companies object to the plan within 30 days. So, companies have until Nov. 3 to object to it.

This is exactly what companies like Tesla and SpaceX did today: exercise their power to protest the tokenized stock plan.

TheStreet Roundtable spoke to Markus Levin, co-founder of XYO, a cryptographic proof network for data and AI, to get insights on the subject.

"I read this as companies objecting to someone else tokenizing their stock rather than to tokenization itself, since a third-party token leaves the issuer with little visibility into who holds its shares or how votes and dividends reach them. "said Levin. I'd expect most of them to tokenize their own stock through their transfer agents once there's a clear standard for keeping the token and the shareholder register in sync," he added.

news.Title: Skyworks Solutions (SWKS) Tops Q4 Earnings and Revenue Estimates
news.Content:
Skyworks Solutions (SWKS) came out with quarterly earnings of $1.28 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $1.27 per share. This compares to earnings of $1.76 per share a year ago. These figures are adjusted for non-recurring items.

This quarterly report represents an earnings surprise of +0.79%. A quarter ago, it was expected that this chipmaker would post earnings of $1.03 per share when it actually produced earnings of $1.08, delivering a surprise of +4.85%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has surpassed consensus EPS estimates four times.

Skyworks, which belongs to the Zacks Semiconductors - Radio Frequency industry, posted revenues of $1.05 billion for the quarter ended September 2026, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 1.49%. This compares to year-ago revenues of $1.1 billion. The company has topped consensus revenue estimates four times over the last four quarters.

The sustainability of the stock's immediate price movement based on the recently-released numbers and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's commentary on the earnings call.

Skyworks shares have added about 34.3% since the beginning of the year versus the S&P 500's gain of 10.2%.

What's Next for Skyworks?

While Skyworks has outperformed the market so far this year, the question that comes to investors' minds is: what's next for the stock?

There are no easy answers to this key question, but one reliable measure that can help investors address this is the company's earnings outlook. Not only does this include current consensus earnings expectations for the coming quarter(s), but also how these expectations have changed lately.

Empirical research shows a strong correlation between near-term stock movements and trends in earnings estimate revisions. Investors can track such revisions by themselves or rely on a tried-and-tested rating tool like the Zacks Rank, which has an impressive track record of harnessing the power of earnings estimate revisions.

Ahead of this earnings release, the estimate revisions trend for Skyworks was mixed. While the magnitude and direction of estimate revisions could change following the company's just-released earnings report, the current status translates into a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) for the stock. So, the shares are expected to perform in line with the market in the near future. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

It will be interesting to see how estimates for the coming quarters and the current fiscal year change in the days ahead. The current consensus EPS estimate is $1.30 on $1.05 billion in revenues for the coming quarter and $5.18 on $4.06 billion in revenues for the current fiscal year.

Investors should be mindful of the fact that the outlook for the industry can have a material impact on the performance of the stock as well. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than 2 to 1.

news.Title: STMicroelectronics Unveils STM32A, Edge AI Chips for Automotive and Robotics
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in STMicroelectronics N.V.? Here are five stocks we like better.

STMicroelectronics introduced the STM32A microcontroller family for automotive and high-safety applications, spanning entry-level vehicle nodes through ASIL D-capable zonal endpoints. The lineup is also intended for industrial automation, robotics, energy systems and infrastructure.

ST launched the STM32G5 and STM32H7P microcontrollers for motor control, digital power, signal processing and edge AI. The H7P combines a Cortex-M7 processor, DSP accelerator and 82-GOPS neural accelerator, while the G5 emphasizes higher performance, advanced peripherals and post-quantum security support.

The company expanded its edge-AI strategy through Arm and NVIDIA partnerships, new STM32Cube development tools and updated AI software for model discovery, customization, benchmarking and data preparation. ST also announced STM32Cube for Agentic AI, designed to help coding assistants use STM32-specific development context.

STMicroelectronics Could Reach New Highs—Here's What Needs to Happen

STMicroelectronics (NYSE:STM) used its STM32 Summit in Silicon Valley to outline a "technology convergence" strategy for embedded systems and introduce new microcontroller families and software tools aimed at automotive, industrial automation, robotics, digital power and edge artificial intelligence applications.

The company said its unified STM32 MCU platform is intended to help developers reuse software, tools and intellectual property across product families and markets as systems become more connected, software-defined, security-focused and capable of autonomous operation. ST said the platform is supported by consistent Arm Cortex-M-based architectures, the STM32Cube ecosystem, shared process technologies and a supply chain it manages internally.

→ L3Harris Stock Took a Beating—Is a 20% Rebound Next?

Apple, Meta, and SpaceX Are Driving a Device Boom—These 3 Stocks Could Benefit

According to the company, the STM32 developer ecosystem includes close to 2 million developers, while its ST Community receives more than 300,000 visitors per month. ST also said it has shipped more than 20 billion STM32 devices.

Arm partnership and physical AI

Arm Executive Vice President of the Physical AI Business Unit Drew Henry said ST will be a lead partner in defining the future Cortex-M roadmap, alongside Cadence as a design partner. Henry said Arm has shipped more than 100 billion Cortex-M devices and sees physical AI as a potential $200 billion compute market by the middle of the next decade.

Story Continues

→ LyondellBasell's Dividend Looks Safer, But a New Risk Could Change That

Industrial Chips Are in Rally Mode—5 Ways to Play

"We believe that this is a $200 billion compute market in the middle of next decade or so," Henry said, referring to systems that apply AI to agriculture, manufacturing, transportation and other real-world environments.

ST said it is combining Arm CPUs, its neural accelerators and more than a decade of MCU AI software experience for edge AI workloads. The company also highlighted deterministic Ethernet connectivity, integrated security features including SHA accelerators and post-quantum cryptography libraries, and safety-focused hardware and software support.

STM32A expands into automotive and safety applications

→ Marvell Eyes a Swing for the AI Networking Fences as Markets Weigh Lumentum Price Tag

A central product announcement was the STM32A series, which ST described as a new line combining its general-purpose and automotive microcontroller experience. The series is designed for automotive and high-safety embedded applications, including industrial automation, robotics, energy systems and infrastructure.

ST unveiled the initial three-product roadmap:

STM32A4: Intended for entry-level automotive nodes, including distributed sensing, actuation, doors, windows, lighting and local controls. ST said the devices will offer low cost, compact memory, cryptographic support and LIN implementation.

STM32A5: Targeted at body and comfort-control functions, with up to 4 MB of memory, enhanced security and safety support up to ASIL B. ST said the devices are also suited to mid-range safety-critical industrial, robotics and energy applications.

STM32A9: Intended for higher-function zonal vehicle endpoints, with real-time control, low-latency and Ethernet-oriented connectivity, plus safety support up to ASIL D. ST said its split-lock core architecture can prioritize ASIL D operation or provide twice the ASIL B performance when ASIL D is not required.

The company said the STM32A family will provide continuity with STM32-compatible IP, software concepts, tools and the STM32Cube ecosystem while addressing automotive-grade qualification, functional safety, security and longer product lifecycles.

NVIDIA Vice President of Robotics and Edge AI Deepu Talla discussed the companies' work around robotics and the Holoscan Sensor Bridge, which enables sensor and actuator connectivity over Ethernet. ST said it plans to release Holoscan Sensor Bridge software as a native component of the STM32Cube ecosystem in coming months and intends to develop simulation libraries for its sensor, MEMS, microcontroller and actuation portfolios.

STM32G5 and STM32H7P product launches

ST also launched the STM32G5, a general-purpose mixed-signal microcontroller based on an Arm Cortex-M33 running at up to 280 MHz. The company said the device delivers a CoreMark score more than double that of the STM32G4 and is designed for motor control and digital power applications.

Versions aimed at digital power will include additional high-resolution timers, while motor-control versions will provide more analog peripherals, ST said. Other cited capabilities include a 111-picosecond timer resolution, a position encoder, a programmable logic array with 16 logic elements, a 5-megasample-per-second analog-to-digital converter and pseudo-differential mode for signal-to-noise performance.

The STM32G5 targets SESIP Level 3 and PSA Certified Level 3 security certifications and supports post-quantum cryptographic libraries, according to ST. Initial devices, Nucleo boards and Discovery kits are available, while ST said a dual-core version is being developed for release next year.

Ram Kumar of ST introduced the STM32H7P, describing it as the company's first STM32H7 combining a Cortex-M7 processor, a Hardware Signal Processor DSP accelerator and an 82-GOPS Neural-ART accelerator. The microcontroller operates at up to 520 MHz and delivers a CoreMark score of nearly 2,700, which Kumar said is 150% above most competing solutions.

The STM32H7P includes high-resolution timers, comparators and twice the flash memory of a 1 MB STM32H7 at roughly the same price, according to ST. Kumar said the device is aimed at digital power, digital signal processing and edge AI applications, and can operate in industrial environments up to 105 degrees Celsius through exposed-pad packaging.

AI development software update

ST also updated its AI software offering. Miguel Castro, head of AI marketing and strategy for the Americas, said the company is replacing its Model Zoo interface with Model Explorer, Model Factory and Model Bench tools for discovering, customizing and benchmarking AI models. It also introduced Dataset Factory for organizing and cleaning data.

In addition, ST announced STM32Cube for Agentic AI, a tool intended to provide coding assistants with STM32 documentation, guidelines, examples and other development context. Castro said early experiments reduced token usage by 93% for a blinking-light application, while typical configurations are expected to reduce token usage by roughly 50% to 60%.

About STMicroelectronics (NYSE:STM)

STMicroelectronics N.V. (NYSE: STM) is a global semiconductor company that designs, develops, manufactures and markets a broad range of integrated circuits and other semiconductor products. Its offerings support applications in automotive, industrial, personal electronics, communications equipment and computer systems.

The company's product portfolio includes microcontrollers, analog and power semiconductors, sensors, microelectromechanical systems (MEMS), connectivity products and automotive chips.

news.Title: Lam Research Sees Strong 2027 Growth as Shareholders Back Board, Pay Plan
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Lam Research Corporation? Here are five stocks we like better.

Shareholders approved all four key voting outcomes: They elected Lam Research's 10 director nominees, approved executive compensation, ratified KPMG as fiscal 2027 auditor, and rejected a proposal to lower the ownership threshold for calling special meetings.

Lam expects strong 2027 semiconductor-equipment demand. The company projects wafer fabrication equipment spending will exceed $200 billion, up about 30%, as 10 major fabs become available to receive equipment and clean-room constraints ease.

CEO Tim Archer cited gate-all-around transistors, EUV and high-NA EUV lithography, backside power delivery, and advanced packaging as long-term growth drivers because these technologies require intensive etch and deposition processes.

Lam Research's Earnings Beat Wasn't the Real Story—Its 2027 Outlook Was

Lam Research (NASDAQ:LRCX) stockholders elected all 10 director nominees, approved the company's executive compensation plan on an advisory basis and ratified KPMG LLP as its independent auditor for fiscal 2027 at the company's 2026 annual meeting.

The virtual meeting, chaired by Board Chair Abhi Talwalkar, did not include a formal business update because Lam had provided its most recent update during its Oct. 21 earnings release call. Talwalkar said the meeting's purpose was to vote on four proposals outlined in the company's proxy materials.

→ L3Harris Stock Took a Beating—Is a 20% Rebound Next?

From High Dividend Growth to High Yield, These 3 Stocks Just Boosted Dividend Payouts

Corporate Secretary Ava Harter reported that a quorum was present. Following the vote, Harter said preliminary results showed that stockholders had:

Elected all 10 board nominees.

Approved the advisory "say-on-pay" vote covering named executive officer compensation.

Ratified KPMG LLP as Lam's independent registered public accounting firm for fiscal 2027.

Rejected a stockholder proposal concerning the right to call special stockholder meetings.

Lam said it expects to report final voting results in a Form 8-K filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission within four business days.

Special Meeting Proposal Rejected

→ LyondellBasell's Dividend Looks Safer, But a New Risk Could Change That

Analysts Just Raised Price Targets On These 3 Semiconductor Equipment Stocks

The shareholder proposal, presented by stockholder John Chevedden, called on Lam's board to amend the company's governing documents to allow holders of a combined 10% of outstanding common stock to call a special stockholder meeting.

Story Continues

Chevedden argued that Lam's current rules create significant barriers by requiring 20% support and excluding a substantial block of shares from being included in the qualifying group. He said the requested change would create an "attainable shareholder right" to call a special meeting.

→ Marvell Eyes a Swing for the AI Networking Fences as Markets Weigh Lumentum Price Tag

Harter said the board recommended that stockholders vote against the proposal for the reasons included in the company's proxy statement. The proposal was not approved.

CEO Cites Demand From Technology Transitions

During a post-meeting question-and-answer session, President and Chief Executive Officer Tim Archer discussed semiconductor technology transitions, including gate-all-around transistor architectures and the implementation of extreme ultraviolet, or EUV, and high-numerical-aperture EUV lithography.

Archer said these transitions are "extremely etch and deposition intensive," making them well suited to Lam's product portfolio and driving significant demand for its equipment.

He also identified backside power delivery and advanced packaging as potential long-term growth drivers. Archer acknowledged that supply-chain issues have constrained the pace of industry growth, but said Lam is working around those challenges.

Fiscal 2027 Industry Outlook

Archer said customer fabrication-plant utilization rates remain very high. He noted that limited clean-room space was one of the constraints on industry growth during the current year because chipmakers needed more space to install equipment and expand production.

That constraint is expected to ease somewhat in 2027, according to Archer, who said Lam expects 10 tier-one fabs to open and become available to receive equipment during the year.

Lam's outlook, as previously discussed on its latest earnings call, calls for wafer fabrication equipment spending to exceed $200 billion in 2027, representing approximately 30% growth from the current year. Archer added that Lam believes its addressable markets are growing faster than the broader semiconductor equipment industry and said 2027 appears positioned to be another strong growth year for the company.

About Lam Research (NASDAQ:LRCX)

Lam Research Corporation (NASDAQ:LRCX) is a semiconductor equipment company that develops and manufactures systems used to fabricate integrated circuits. Its technologies support key stages of wafer processing, helping semiconductor manufacturers create the increasingly complex structures found in memory, logic and other types of chips.

The company's product portfolio includes etch systems, which selectively remove materials from wafers; deposition systems, which apply thin films; and cleaning solutions used to remove contaminants and residue during manufacturing.

news.Title: Marvell gives up a third of itself to buy its laser supplier
news.Content:
Last week, I described a fading rally in Lumentum Holdings ( LITE ) shares as the market marking down a takeover premium in real time. On Monday, November 2, 2026, Marvell Technology ( MRVL ) made it official. The markdown has gone further than the headline price suggests.

Marvell agreed to buy the laser maker in an all-stock deal valued at $115 billion, according to a press release . Lumentum holders will receive 4.5 Marvell shares for each share they own.

Marvell's current owners will hold about 67% of the combined company after closing, the companies said. In other words, Marvell is handing a third of itself to Lumentum's shareholders.

Also read: Marvell may buy its own laser supplier as investors pull back

That split is fixed. The dollar value Lumentum's holders will receive is not fixed, and Marvell's falling stock has reduced it.

Marvell's slide has already erased the deal premium

The press release values the offer at about $1,132 per Lumentum share. The price reflects a 23.9% premium, based on both stocks' closing prices on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, before deal talk began.

Marvell shares fell about 22% between the leak and the close on Friday, October 30, 2026, partly on a broad chip selloff, according to Reuters .

By my math, a Marvell decline of about 19% wipes out that premium. At Friday's close, 4.5 Marvell shares were worth roughly $884, below Lumentum's implied pre-leak price of about $914.

The premium was gone before the deal was announced. On deal day, Marvell shares fell about 10%, and Lumentum dropped about 15% in afternoon trading.

Lumentum falling harder than its buyer stands out. By my math, Lumentum's discount to the offer's value roughly doubled from Friday. To me, that gap is the market's price for waiting until 2028 and for the risk that regulators say no.

Marvell CEO Matt Murphy sees it differently. "Whether we're trading at $180 or $280," he told Fox Business , the agreed ownership split "is very, very compelling for Lumentum shareholders."

He said the split came from him and Lumentum CEO Michael Hurlston "haggling it out" until the terms were "high for me and too low for him."

Lumentum is growing faster than the company buying it

Lumentum's latest quarter suggests Hurlston had plenty to haggle with. He said in the same interview that the results, released three days early , had "gotten lost in the backwash."

Revenue jumped about 136% from a year earlier to $1.26 billion, according to Lumentum's earnings release . By comparison, Marvell's revenue grew 37% in its latest full quarter, according to its August earnings release . Lumentum is growing more than three times as fast.

Story Continues

More importantly, Hurlston said in the release that Lumentum secured its second major win in near-packaged and co-packaged optics. That win is "backed by purchase commitments exceeding $5 billion," he said.

Those designs put optics beside or inside the chip package. That commitment matters more than the earnings beat. It shows Marvell is buying contracted demand.

Marvell's promised savings come from the factory floor

That demand only rewards Marvell's owners if margins follow. The investor presentation puts the combined non-GAAP gross margin at 57%. Marvell's own is 58%, so the deal starts by diluting it.

The fix is more than $1 billion in yearly cost savings, mostly from cost of goods sold, according to the presentation. In plain terms, that means cheaper production.

By my math, those savings equal more than 5% of the presentation's $17.7 billion in combined annualized revenue. Savings of that size would lift the combined gross margin above Marvell's standalone level.

Yet that payoff waits on a closing expected in the first half of 2028, the press release said. Meanwhile, here is where last week's three questions stand:

The exchange ratio is settled, handing Lumentum holders about a third of the company.

Adjusted earnings of $4.57 per share beat the $4.22 analysts expected, according to Seeking Alpha .

Cloud Light, the Lumentum module unit that competes with some Marvell chip customers, goes unmentioned in Monday's press release and presentation.

Murphy's words sharpen that last risk. He said the combined company could go from "selling an individual component" to selling "an entire module."

He meant new scale-up designs, but many of Marvell's chip customers build modules. Last week, I wanted the terms before adding Marvell. Now that comment keeps me on the sidelines for both stocks.

More Marvell:

Marvell may buy its own laser supplier as investors pull back

Bank of America tweaks Marvell stock target after key Analyst Day

Marvell just made a move that changes the AI networking story

Marvell's deals keep moving deeper into optics

The bigger question is what kind of company Marvell becomes. The Lumentum deal is more than 10 times Marvell's previous biggest purchase, the $10 billion Inphi buyout in 2021, according to Reuters . Inphi made electro-optics products, according to a Marvell press release .

In February 2026, Marvell completed its purchase of Celestial AI, which it called "a pioneer in optical interconnect technology." Lumentum goes further, giving Marvell the lasers and the plants that make them.

However, paying in stock makes the buyer's share price the real price tag. "You take more risk when you do it," Murphy said. Marvell has more than a year to prove its shares are worth the third it is giving away.

More Stocks News

Ford and GM see savings drivers may pay for later

Mark Cuban says get your cash ready for this change — 'That's when the real money is made'

Michael Burry's favorite stock gets a 26% Morgan Stanley reset

Rivian car buyers are driving a Wall Street rethink on the stock

news.Title: SIMO Earnings Surge as Enterprise and AI Storage Drive New Momentum
news.Content:
Silicon Motion Technology Corporation SIMO delivered a sharp third-quarter earnings acceleration as enterprise, automotive and artificial intelligence storage became larger contributors to growth. The results strengthen the case that its revenue mix is moving beyond traditional consumer storage controllers.

The key question is whether that shift can support a more durable earnings profile. Current guidance, expanding solutions revenue and new enterprise products point to broader growth drivers, though execution and consumer-market risks remain.

SIMO's Third Quarter Set New Financial Highs

Third-quarter 2026 revenues reached $560.2 million, up 131% year over year and 24% sequentially. Non-GAAP earnings of $4.35 per American depositary share beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $3.30 by 31.82% and increased 335% from the year-ago period.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Profitability also improved materially. Non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 32.1% from 15.8% a year earlier, while gross margin rose to 53.7% from 48.7%. The combination of higher volumes and a richer product mix helped lift operating leverage.

Silicon Motion's Solutions Business is Surging

Ferri and boot-drive solution sales climbed 75-80% sequentially in the third quarter, supported by automotive, edge artificial intelligence and enterprise demand. Solutions accounted for more than 40% of total revenues, and management expects the category could represent roughly half of revenues in 2027.

That mix shift could make Silicon Motion less dependent on consumer controller cycles. Automotive programs generally span three to five years, while enterprise boot-drive opportunities provide another source of longer-duration demand. Micron Technology, Inc. MU is also expanding high-capacity data-center solid-state drive offerings for artificial intelligence, cloud and hyperscale workloads, underscoring the broader storage opportunity tied to data-intensive computing.

SIMO's Fourth-Quarter Guidance Extends the Trend

Management expects fourth-quarter revenues of $588 million to $616 million, implying sequential growth of 5%-10%. Non-GAAP gross margin is projected at 54%-55%, while operating margin is expected to reach 36%-37%.

The outlook suggests the third-quarter improvement is carrying into year-end rather than fading immediately after a record period. For 2027, management expects revenue growth of at least 40% and gross margins in the low-to-mid-50% range, supported by rising contributions from enterprise controllers and Ferri automotive solutions.

Story Continues

Silicon Motion Is Building for the Next AI Cycle

Silicon Motion taped out its 4-nanometer PCIe Gen6 MonTitan controller in the third quarter, with sampling scheduled for the first quarter of 2027. The product targets hyperscalers and cloud service providers and is designed for both TLC-based compute storage and QLC-based data storage.

Four NAND makers have begun producing 2-terabit QLC dies, with broader availability expected by the end of 2027. That supply expansion could support higher-capacity enterprise storage deployments. Seagate Technology Holdings plc STX is likewise positioning its mass-capacity storage portfolio around rising artificial intelligence and cloud data demand, showing that infrastructure spending is broadening across storage technologies.

SIMO's Ratings Temper the Earnings Excitement

The latest quarter supports the view that Silicon Motion is becoming a more diversified storage supplier, but the transition is not yet complete. Consumer weakness, customer qualification requirements and supply-chain constraints still create uncertainty around how smoothly the enterprise ramp develops.

SIMO currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). It also has a Value Score of D and Momentum Score of D, along with a Growth Score of F and VGM Score of F. Because the Style Scores complement the Zacks Rank, these weaker grades suggest a more measured near-term stance even as the company's enterprise and artificial intelligence exposure expands. news.Title: SIMO Stock Falls 33.5% in a Month as Growth Meets Execution Risks
news.Content:
Silicon Motion Technology Corporation SIMO shares have fallen 33.5% over the past four weeks, a sharp reversal despite record revenues and expanding exposure to enterprise and AI storage. The drop raises the question of whether valuation now better reflects the company's growth prospects.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The answer is not straightforward. Enterprise diversification, automotive demand and higher-value storage products support the outlook, but consumer weakness, qualification requirements and supply-chain constraints leave execution risk elevated.

SIMO's Record Growth Contrasts With the Sell-Off

Third-quarter 2026 revenues surged 131% year over year to about $560 million, marking a fourth consecutive quarter of record revenues. Non-GAAP earnings per ADS rose 335% to $4.35, while operating margin expanded to 32.1%.

The quarter also exceeded the Zacks Consensus Estimate on both the top and bottom lines. Management expects fourth-quarter revenues of $588-$616 million, with non-GAAP operating margin rising to 36%-37%.

Silicon Motion's Enterprise Mix Is Expanding

Ferri automotive and enterprise boot-drive solutions grew more than 75% sequentially and represented more than 40% of third-quarter revenues. Management indicated that the solutions business could reach roughly half of revenues in 2027.

That shift increases exposure to longer-duration programs and higher-value storage opportunities. Micron Technology, Inc. MU, which offers DRAM, NAND and data-center SSDs, illustrates the broader memory and storage ecosystem in which enterprise demand is expanding.

SIMO Faces Persistent Consumer Pressure

Elevated NAND and DRAM prices are pressuring smartphone and PC affordability. eMMC and UFS controller revenues declined modestly sequentially in the third quarter, and management expects near-term revenues in that business to remain relatively flat.

SSD controller revenues are also expected to be flat to slightly lower sequentially in the fourth quarter. These trends show that enterprise growth is offsetting, rather than eliminating, weakness in established consumer-facing markets.

Silicon Motion Must Execute on Enterprise Ramps

Enterprise expansion depends on customer qualifications, production ramps and component availability. MonTitan is scaling across seven announced customers, while Silicon Motion's 4-nanometer PCIe Gen6 MonTitan controller is scheduled to begin sampling in the first quarter of 2027.

Near-CPU boot-drive opportunities add another execution layer because customized firmware and customer-specific features are required. Seagate Technology Holdings PLC STX, whose portfolio includes cloud, edge and data-center storage products, provides another reference point for the scale and complexity of enterprise storage markets.

Story Continues

SIMO's Valuation Adds Context to the Decline

SIMO trades at 12.1X forward 12-month earnings, below its five-year median of 19.4X but above the Zacks sub-industry's 9.4X. The lower multiple versus its own history reflects a materially different valuation backdrop after the recent share-price pullback.

The discount to SIMO's historical median may look more attractive if enterprise ramps progress as planned. Still, the premium to the sub-industry means investors are not being offered a uniformly cheap valuation relative to peers.

SIMO's Signals Still Favor a Cautious View

SIMO's growth and valuation setup remains mixed. Record operating performance and enterprise diversification support the longer-term case, while consumer pressure and execution requirements argue against treating the 33.5% decline alone as a buy signal.

The stock currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). It has a Value Score of D and Momentum Score of D, along with a Growth Score of F and VGM Score of F. Since the Style Scores are designed to complement the Zacks Rank, these weaker grades support a measured stance despite the company's strong recent fundamental growth. Meanwhile, software firm Skyworks Solutions SWKS reports its fiscal Q4 report after today's close. Following the company's $10 billion Qorvo acquisition, Skyworks looks to report earning down -27.84% year over year, -6.35% on revenues. The company has not missed on bottom-line estimates since Q1 2019.

Story Continues

What to Expect from the Stock Market Today

We won't get any midterm returns until well after today's trading session is over, but we'll make sure to keep abreast of developments throughout the country today. Otherwise, the September print on Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey (JOLTS) is expected to remain in-line with the prior month, at +7.1 million job openings.

JOLTS numbers are back to pre-Covid levels, and have been here pretty steadily over the past nearly two years. This is consistent with the "low hire/low fire" employment numbers we've seen elsewhere. Job Quits in August dropped to 3.07 million, at an historically low +1.9% rate. Basically, lots of people remain employed, but fewer are finding opportunities elsewhere. Today's JOLTS figures kicks off the latest "Jobs Week."

news.Title: Silicon Motion Technology Corporation (SIMO) is Attracting Investor Attention: Here is What You Should Know
news.Content:
Silicon Motion (SIMO) is one of the stocks most watched by Zacks.com visitors lately. So, it might be a good idea to review some of the factors that might affect the near-term performance of the stock.

Over the past month, shares of this chip company have returned -33.5%, compared to the Zacks S&P 500 composite's -2.3% change. During this period, the Zacks Computer - Integrated Systems industry, which Silicon Motion falls in, has lost 21.9%. The key question now is: What could be the stock's future direction?

While media releases or rumors about a substantial change in a company's business prospects usually make its stock 'trending' and lead to an immediate price change, there are always some fundamental facts that eventually dominate the buy-and-hold decision-making.

Revisions to Earnings Estimates

Rather than focusing on anything else, we at Zacks prioritize evaluating the change in a company's earnings projection. This is because we believe the fair value for its stock is determined by the present value of its future stream of earnings.

We essentially look at how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to reflect the impact of the latest business trends. And if earnings estimates go up for a company, the fair value for its stock goes up. A higher fair value than the current market price drives investors' interest in buying the stock, leading to its price moving higher. This is why empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

Silicon Motion is expected to post earnings of $4.75 per share for the current quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +277%. Over the last 30 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate has changed +13.1%.

The consensus earnings estimate of $12.91 for the current fiscal year indicates a year-over-year change of +263.7%. This estimate has changed -5.5% over the last 30 days.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $19.86 indicates a change of +53.9% from what Silicon Motion is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has changed +28.5%.

With an impressive externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool -- the Zacks Rank -- is a more conclusive indicator of a stock's near-term price performance, as it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. The size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) for Silicon Motion.

Story Continues

The chart below shows the evolution of the company's forward 12-month consensus EPS estimate:

12 Month EPS

Revenue Growth Forecast

While earnings growth is arguably the most superior indicator of a company's financial health, nothing happens as such if a business isn't able to grow its revenues. After all, it's nearly impossible for a company to increase its earnings for an extended period without increasing its revenues. So, it's important to know a company's potential revenue growth.

In the case of Silicon Motion, the consensus sales estimate of $602.1 million for the current quarter points to a year-over-year change of +116.2%. The $1.94 billion and $2.72 billion estimates for the current and next fiscal years indicate changes of +118.8% and +40.6%, respectively.

Last Reported Results and Surprise History

Silicon Motion reported revenues of $560.22 million in the last reported quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +131.5%. EPS of $4.35 for the same period compares with $1 a year ago.

Compared to the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $532.81 million, the reported revenues represent a surprise of +5.14%. The EPS surprise was +31.82%.

Over the last four quarters, Silicon Motion surpassed consensus EPS estimates three times. The company topped consensus revenue estimates each time over this period.

Valuation

Without considering a stock's valuation, no investment decision can be efficient. In predicting a stock's future price performance, it's crucial to determine whether its current price correctly reflects the intrinsic value of the underlying business and the company's growth prospects.

While comparing the current values of a company's valuation multiples, such as price-to-earnings (P/E), price-to-sales (P/S), and price-to-cash flow (P/CF), with its own historical values helps determine whether its stock is fairly valued, overvalued, or undervalued, comparing the company relative to its peers on these parameters gives a good sense of the reasonability of the stock's price.

The Zacks Value Style Score (part of the Zacks Style Scores system), which pays close attention to both traditional and unconventional valuation metrics to grade stocks from A to F (an A is better than a B; a B is better than a C; and so on), is pretty helpful in identifying whether a stock is overvalued, rightly valued, or temporarily undervalued.

Silicon Motion is graded D on this front, indicating that it is trading at a premium to its peers. Click here to see the values of some of the valuation metrics that have driven this grade.

Bottom Line

The facts discussed here and much other information on Zacks.com might help determine whether or not it's worthwhile paying attention to the market buzz about Silicon Motion. However, its Zacks Rank #3 does suggest that it may perform in line with the broader market in the near term.

news.Title: ASML Surges 48% in the Past Year: How Should You Play the Stock Now?
news.Content:
ASML Holding N.V. ASML has gained 48.1% over the past year compared with the sector's growth of 9.5%. It has outperformed Advanced Energy Industries, Inc. AEIS but lagged Silicon Motion Technology Corporation SIMO. While AEIS has gained 11.4%, SIMO soared 103.6% over this period.

One-Year ASML Stock Price Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

ASML Rides on Strong AI Demand

ASML is benefiting from growing AI infrastructure investments, which are encouraging leading semiconductor manufacturers to expand their production capabilities. The company's Installed Base Management revenues reached €3.29 billion in the third quarter of 2026, increasing from €2.76 billion in the preceding quarter, driven by strong demand for productivity upgrades. New lithography system sales increased to 113 units from 86 in the second quarter.

Management highlighted improving order momentum, with some customers expressing interest in placing equipment orders for 2029 and 2030. The combination of capacity growth and higher lithography content gives ASML multiple structural avenues for revenue expansion through 2026 and beyond.

The company's dominant position in extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography technology provides a competitive advantage, particularly as chipmakers expand production of advanced logic and memory chips. ASML's expanding technological capabilities, strategic partnerships and improving financial outlook further strengthen its investment appeal. The company is advancing High Numerical Aperture (High-NA) EUV technology, which is expected to support next-generation semiconductor manufacturing and drive long-term equipment demand. Its expanding collaborations with Intel, Samsung and TSMC reinforce its position in advanced chipmaking.

Estimate Revision Trend

Earnings estimates for ASML for 2026 have moved up 54.4% to $46.54 over the past year, while the same for 2027 has increased 61.9% to $62.54. The positive estimate revision depicts bullish sentiment about the stock's growth potential.

ASML Growth Marred by Long Order Visibility

Despite the positives, management attributes the current demand environment primarily to AI-related investment and the resulting need for more advanced Logic and Memory capacity. This has produced unusually long order visibility for ASML, but it also makes the growth profile increasingly dependent on customers maintaining those expansion plans. A slower pace of customer investment would therefore affect both system demand and utilization of the larger production footprint ASML is preparing.

The planned scale-up requires manufacturing capacity, suppliers and trained employees to rise together. This leaves future profitability dependent on converting the larger cost base into the expected shipment volumes. Moreover, a uniform adoption schedule across Logic and DRAM customers is yet to be established. High-NA therefore remains both a technology opportunity and an execution variable, with the pace of wider insertion dependent on customer qualification and manufacturing decisions rather than ASML's roadmap alone.

Story Continues

Other Headwinds

ASML also faces operational challenges related to capacity expansion, supply-chain constraints and the growing complexity of its advanced lithography systems. In its third-quarter 2026 update, management indicated that planned production capacity for 2027 and 2028 would not fully meet anticipated customer demand, highlighting potential execution risks as the company scales manufacturing operations. Expanding capacity requires substantial investments, specialized components and a highly skilled workforce, while supplier bottlenecks could delay system deliveries and revenue recognition. In addition, developing and commercializing next-generation High-NA EUV technology requires significant R&D spending that could weigh on ASML's growth prospects.

End Note

ASML's technological leadership in EUV lithography, healthy order trends and expanding installed-base revenues reinforce its long-term investment appeal. With upward earnings estimate revisions, the stock is witnessing positive investor sentiment. However, export-control uncertainties, capacity-expansion challenges and long order visibility remain headwinds.

Stiff competitive pressure and supply-chain bottlenecks also plague the company's growth prospects. High operating and R&D expenses remain an overhang as well. With a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), ASML appears to be treading in the middle of the road, and investors could be better off if they trade with caution. news.Title: Should You Trade SIMO Stock With Caution Despite Q3 Earnings Beat?
news.Content:
Silicon Motion Technology Corporation SIMO reported strong third-quarter 2026 results, with both the top and bottom lines surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate. Non-GAAP earnings of $4.35 per American Depositary Share (ADS) increased 335% year over year and beat the consensus estimate of $3.30 by 31.82%.

Revenues surged 131% year over year to approximately $560 million, exceeding the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $533 million by 5.07%. Growth was supported by robust demand for SSD controllers and Ferri & Boot Drive solutions, with the latter witnessing a remarkable 2,580-2,585% year-over-year sales increase.

SIMO Buoyed by Healthy Demand Trends

Silicon Motion is witnessing solid growth dynamics driven by strong momentum in enterprise and edge SSD controllers, automotive storage solutions and enterprise boot drive products. SSD controller sales increased 55-60% year over year and 20-25% sequentially, benefiting from expanding demand for edge and enterprise storage applications. Sales of embedded Multi-Media Card and Universal Flash Storage (eMMC+UFS) controllers rose 35-40% year over year.

Ferri & Boot Drive solutions sales increased 75-80% sequentially, supported by rapid adoption of automotive, edge artificial intelligence (AI) and enterprise boot drive solutions. Management highlighted growing contributions from its MonTitan enterprise and AI controllers as the company expands beyond traditional consumer storage markets.

Fabless Business Model Aids SIMO

Silicon Motion operates a fabless business model, focusing on chip design while outsourcing manufacturing to foundries like TSMC. Consequently, the company has a low capital investment requirement as it does not require expensive fabrication plants, enabling it to adopt advanced manufacturing nodes quickly, leading to higher margins compared to integrated manufacturers. This enables the company to focus on innovation and product development rather than manufacturing complexity.

The key growth drivers for SIMO include AI and high-performance computing, cloud data centers, automotive storage, smartphones and mobile devices. Each of these end markets is growing fast and offers lucrative growth potential. An expanding customer base and innovative products will likely act as tailwinds for the company's top-line growth. Silicon Motion has shipped more than 10 billion NAND flash controllers in its operating history, with more than 750 million NAND controllers on average every year.

Price Performance

SIMO has gained 103.6% over the past year compared with the industry's growth of 101.5%. It has also outperformed peers like Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. AMD and International Business Machines Corporation IBM. Advanced Micro has gained 86.7%, while IBM is down 16.1% over this period.

Story Continues

One-Year SIMO Stock Price Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Stiff Competition, Geopolitical Issues Hurt SIMO

Despite the positives, Silicon Motion faces stiff competition in the mobile storage market from players like Micron, Microchip, Marvell and ON Semiconductor. Of late, intensifying competition in the card and USB flash drive controller markets is proving to be a major headwind. The tense political conditions between Taiwan and the People's Republic of China increase the extent of political risk for the company. Moreover, North Korea's nuclear and ballistic missile testing programs, deteriorating relationship with South Korea, leadership woes and strained relations with the United States are likely to affect its business. In addition, high R&D costs have adversely impacted its margins.

Estimate Revision Trend

Earnings estimates for SIMO for 2026 have moved up 164.5% to $12.91 over the past year, while the same for 2027 has increased 203.7% to $19.86. The positive estimate revision depicts bullish sentiment about the stock's growth potential.

End Note

With solid fundamentals and healthy revenue-generating potential, driven by robust demand trends, Silicon Motion is poised for long-term growth. Further, a strong emphasis on quality, diligent execution of operational plans and continuous portfolio enhancements are driving more value for customers. An asset-light fabless semiconductor model, solid growth exposure to AI, cloud and automotive markets, increasing market share in SSD and mobile controllers and continuous innovation in storage technologies are key growth drivers for the company. With upward earnings estimate revisions, the stock is witnessing positive investor sentiment.

However, stiff competition and supply chain issues are likely to put pressure on the bottom-line growth. High R&D costs erode its profitability to a large extent. Silicon Motion is facing a tough operating environment amid tense geopolitical conditions across the globe. With a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), Silicon Motion appears to be treading in the middle of the road, and investors could be better off if they trade with caution. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

news.Title: 華邦電法說會》總座示警第4季營運恐降溫 分析師：記憶體榮景恐要結束
news.Content:
記憶體大廠華邦電（2344）第三季財報表現強勁，單季大賺354.22億元且EPS衝上7.58元，但公司警示第四季受PC等消費性需求放緩影響，營運動能將不如前幾季。分析師坦言「記憶體族群的派對恐怕即將結束」，雖然短線因先前股價修正過後可能出現跌深反彈，但後續恐難再重演先前的強勁漲勢。

記憶體大廠華邦電（2344）3日公布第三季財報，單季大賺354.22億元年增1103.5%，EPS衝上7.58元。

華邦電總經理陳沛銘於法說會指出，目前產業呈「AI強、非AI弱」雙軌分化。受到PC等消費性客戶第四季拉貨動能放緩影響，第四季營運成長力道將不如前幾季，但長線來看，2027年記憶體缺貨情況恐比今年更為嚴峻，獲利動能依然無虞。

回顧台股3日重挫逾1600點拖累，記憶體指標股同步受壓。隨著華邦電警示第四季旺季不旺，市場高度關心4日股價開盤表現及產業循環高點是否已現。 記憶體族群近期走勢分歧，市場高度關注產業景氣是否已步入循環高點？對此，資深台股分析師蔡明翰指出，「party恐怕快要結束。」

蔡明翰說明，當蘋果（Apple）開始將上游零組件成本轉嫁給消費者，這正宣告記憶體產業的「榮景派對」恐面臨轉折，基本面再向上突破的難度大增。投資人操作上應把握「反彈分批減碼」原則，避免在低點急於殺低。

蔡明翰補充，記憶體此前受惠於價格上揚與備貨潮，帶動相關概念股強勢上攻。隨著供應鏈成本大幅增加，指標性廠商蘋果已被迫透過調漲終端產品售價來轉嫁成本。這意味著消費端承受度將面臨考驗，一旦終端銷售動能受阻，上游零組件的拉貨力道必然隨之放緩，成為記憶體市況高點反轉的關鍵前哨警訊。

「華邦電示警第 4 季營運放緩 ， 驗證基本面疲態。」蔡明翰進一步指出，華邦電第四季營運動能出現放緩跡象，顯示終端需求降溫已開始侵蝕業者營運表現。在缺乏更強勁的基本面利多支撐下，記憶體族群後續營運要再創造超預期的爆發性成長，難度相當高。

針對近期記憶體族群的急跌走勢，蔡明翰認為，股價短線遭遇重挫後，技術面已呈超跌態勢，隨時有機會迎來技術性反彈。因此，投資人在操作上「切勿在低點急於砍單」，應靜待個股回溫反彈時，再採取「逢高逐步減碼」的應對策略，以控制投資組合風險。

news.Title: 〈華邦電法說〉明年記憶體供給恐比今年更吃緊 斥731億元擴建高雄廠
news.Content:
華邦電(2344-TW)今(3)日召開法說，經營團隊認為，明年記憶體供給仍相當吃緊，甚至可能比今年更緊俏，預計狀況延續到2028年；為因應後續需求，華邦電董事會也通過731億元資本支出案，主要用於高雄廠Module B擴建。

華邦電表示，除了AI伺服器外，Edge AI、車用及基礎建設等應用也將持續帶動記憶體需求，尤其DDR3、DDR4及LPDDR4等成熟製程產品，隨部分大廠減少供應，華邦電將持續滿足長期合作客戶需求。

產能規劃方面，華邦電高雄Module A廠目前月產能約16K，預計今年底提升至24K，屆時產能將達滿載，2027及2028年也預計維持在24K。至於Module B廠，規劃產能約為Module A的兩倍，預估可達50K至60K，並將採用16奈米製程，提高單位產能的位元產出。

華邦電預計12月29日舉行Module B動工儀式，目標2029年下半年開始少量出貨，2030年逐步開出完整產能。目前已與多家客戶洽談長期供貨合約(LTA)，提前確保2029年以後的產能需求，部分客戶甚至已針對未來LPDDR5等產品提出合作規劃。

此外，華邦電也持續推進16奈米製程，目前月產能約2K，預計逐步擴增至16K，2027年1月起增加投片，經過約半年製程週期後，預期明年下半年可望放量，屆時16奈米產品營收占比有機會超過40%，主要支援DDR4及LPDDR4需求。

資本支出方面，華邦電原預估2026年全年記憶體資本支出約395億元，主要投入晶圓生產製造，約占95%；此次董事會通過的731億元則是針對高雄Module B所需的新增投資規劃，包括廠房土建、機電設備及記憶體製程設備等，兩者涵蓋範圍及用途不同。

news.Title: 外資狠砍1073億元創史上第八大賣超 瞄準主動式ETF減碼、這2檔記憶體同遭砍
news.Content:

news.Title: 〈華邦電法說〉Q3大賺354億元季增45%、EPS 7.58元 Q4營運續向上
news.Content:
華邦電(2344-TW)今(3)日召開法說並公告第三季財報，稅後純益354.22億元，季增45.7%、年增11倍，每股純益7.58元，累計前三季每股純益15.32元。展望第四季，雖然消費性電子需求略有修正，但受惠AI相關需求仍強勁，公司預期整體營運仍可成長。

華邦電指出，第四季市場呈現兩極化，AI相關需求持續強勁，但非AI應用受到消費性電子及PC客戶經過前三季備貨後調整拉貨影響，需求相對疲弱；不過，隨部分客戶合約陸續到期，第四季DRAM報價預期仍有調漲空間，只是漲幅可能不如第三季。

華邦電第三季營收823.31億元，季增37.6%、年增278%；毛利率70.6%，季增4個百分點、年增24個百分點、營益率53.2%、季增5個百分點、年增36個百分點。

華邦電表示，第三季營收成長主要來自記憶體業務，其中客製化記憶體(CMS)占合併營收比重已提升至58%、Flash占32%，邏輯IC則降至9%；單看記憶體事業，第三季營收達742.84億元，毛利率達73.9%，營業利益率達59.8%，產能利用率也已接近100%，成為帶動整體獲利成長的主要動能。

進一步觀察產品表現，第三季CMS(客製化記憶體解決方案)營收季增50%，位元出貨量略減，但平均銷售單價(ASP)大漲約60%；Flash營收則季增34%，位元出貨量大致持平，ASP也成長逾30%。華邦電指出，CMS出貨量略減，主要是預留部分產能給長期合作客戶，以因應後續產能需求。

應用別方面，網通應用營收季增55%，占記憶體事業營收比重31%，主要受惠AI伺服器機櫃內的交換器及網路設備需求增加；電腦應用營收季增66%，占比由第二季15%提升至17%，此外，車用及工業應用營收季增36%，消費性電子也成長35%，占比分別為26%。

news.Title: 華邦電通過731億元資本支出　高雄新廠擬12/29動工
news.Content:
（中央社記者張建中台北2026年11月3日電）記憶體廠華邦電 (2344) 董事會今天通過新台幣731.63億元資本支出，將用於擴建高雄廠廠房及購置生產設備，總經理陳沛銘表示，高雄廠模組B將於12月29日動工，希望2年內可以開始裝機。

華邦電今天召開法人說明會，陳沛銘指出，高雄廠模組A預計今年底月產能擴增到2.4萬至2.5萬片規模，2027年及2028年將維持月產能2.4萬至2.5萬片。

陳沛銘說，董事會今天核准731.63億元資本支出，將用於高雄廠模組B建廠及購置生產設備，預計12月29日舉行簡單動工儀式，希望2年內可以開始裝機，2029年小量產，2030年較大量貢獻產能。

陳沛銘表示，人工智慧（AI）市場需求依然強勁，不過，第4季消費性市場恐面臨修正。AI將成為人類生活不可或缺的一部分，預期AI不會泡沫，只是可能會加速洗牌，部分廠商的投資會泡沫。

陳沛銘指出，華邦電目前居全球編碼型快閃記憶體（NOR Flash）龍頭，單層式儲存型快閃記憶體（SLCNAND Flash）為世界第3，隨著大廠陸續淡出市場，華邦電可望擴展市場，將朝向全球SLC NAND Flash龍頭目標邁進。

至於客製化記憶體方面，陳沛銘說，華邦電將以DDR4及LPDDR4產品為發展重心。

至於產品價格走勢，陳沛銘表示，目前動態隨機存取記憶體（DRAM）價格已高，不過，不至於會下跌。Flash產品價格仍有往上空間，尤其是高容量。

受惠客製化記憶體與Flash產品價格上漲，華邦電第3季營收攀高至新台幣823.31億元，季增37.6%，毛利率70.6%，較第2季上揚4個百分點，歸屬母公司淨利354.22億元，季增45.7%，每股純益7.58元，累計前3季每股純益15.32元。

news.Title: 華邦電Q4消費性需求修正，惟合約價續漲10~20%
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-11-03 17:37:09 周佩宇 發佈

華邦電(2344)總經理陳沛銘(附圖)今(3)日指出，今(2026)年第四季DRAM及Flash價格均可望續漲，漲幅約10%至20%，並看好2027年、2028年營運優於2026年。對2029年新產能開出的下半年也持樂觀看法，但仍須觀察屆時市況；以目前客戶需求來看，即使高雄廠Module B各階段產能全部開出，供給仍可能不足。儘管2026年第四季手機、家電及消費型筆電需求較弱、客戶整理庫存，華邦仍傾向保留產品予長約客戶。

為降低新產能開出後的需求風險，華邦也洽談長期供貨合作，選擇產品路線相符的策略客戶，涵蓋2029年新產能開出後至2032年的需求，目前有意洽談者已超過10家。合作模式包含客戶支付預付款或訂金，支應設備投資，再由未來產品供應回饋，各家條件分別協商。陳沛銘強調，除當下需求，也重視客戶長期產品規劃，例如車用客戶由LPDDR4逐步轉向LPDDR5，就與華邦後續布局較為契合；標準型DDR5則不會積極搶進，大廠轉向DDR5後留下的DDR4供給缺口，仍有可觀市場。

擴產方面，董事會此次通過的731億元投資，包含Module B土建、機電與長交期設備，尚未納入全部正常及短交期設備，後續仍將分階段追加，並非一次建滿月產6萬片。Module B預計年底動土，2029年開出新產能，產品將由16奈米DDR4往14奈米及更先進製程推進，後續亦規劃購買EUV設備。既有Module A由月產1.6萬片擴至2.4萬片的設備正陸續交付，成為2027年資本支出重點；2027年現金基礎資本支出將高於2026年的395億元，Module B此次核准的731億元投資，也有部分款項會到2028年底支付。華邦也持續向政府尋求新用地，評估下一階段擴產，但地點與時程尚未確定。

新業務方面，矽電容已小量出貨，初期規劃的幾千片產能已售罄，正持續擴充供給，並已有大型MLCC廠商採用；陳沛銘表示，目前對華邦整體營收貢獻仍有限，後續將推進更高電容密度產品。CUBE則預計2027年量產，客戶主力為AI ASIC，多用於推論，已有客戶提出四層堆疊及與SoC整合的需求。

news.Title: 華邦電看明後年供需維持緊張，砸731億元續擴產
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-11-03 17:23:58 周佩宇 發佈

華邦電(2344)今(3)日召開法說會，總經理陳沛銘(附圖中)看好記憶體供需持續緊俏，第四季客製化記憶體（CMS）合約價格仍有上漲空間，同時高容量NOR Flash價格上行趨勢可望延續至明(2027)年；他並指出，業界普遍認為2027年供需將比2026年更緊，2028年可能維持相近程度。

華邦電第三季合併營收823.31億元、季增37.6%，毛利率70.6%、季增逾4個百分點，歸屬母公司稅後淨利354.22億元、季增45.7%，每股盈餘7.58元；前三季累計每股盈餘15.32元。董事會今日也通過上半年度股利政策，每股將配發2元現金股利。

產品方面，第三季CMS營收季增50%、占合併營收58%，混合平均售價季增近60%，位元出貨量則季減高個位數百分比，20奈米DDR4、LPDDR4仍為主要成長動能；Flash營收季增34%、占比32%，位元出貨量季持平、混合平均售價季增約三成，其中24奈米營收貢獻提高，高容量NOR營收與出貨占比同步創高。展望2027年，高容量NOR供給持續吃緊，SLC NAND亦有新案導入支撐價格；AI伺服器、車用及基礎架構需求延續，DDR3、DDR4缺貨也帶來過去未有合作的基礎架構客戶。

目前華邦電DRAM在PC與伺服器的銷售規模仍小，陳沛銘預期2027年將明顯成長，尤其看好伺服器需求，電腦應用占記憶體營收比重可望較第三季17%明顯提高；車用則是AI之外較有掌握的成長領域，客戶產品替換不易，長期供貨需求持續。

為因應長期需求，華邦電董事會通過731億元資本支出案，主要投入高雄廠Module B建設與設備，預計12月底動土，目標兩年內完成裝機，無塵室規劃月產能5萬至6萬片。高雄廠既有Module A產能已滿，2027年、2028年月產能維持約2.4萬片，在新產能到位前，公司須提前保留部分產品與庫存，以履行長期供貨安排，Module B長期供貨協議（LTA）也持續洽談。

製程升級方面，16奈米已開始放量，預期2027年帶來顯著營收貢獻，陳沛銘看好2027年下半年占比進一步提高；2027年產品仍聚焦DDR4、LPDDR4，並持續供應DDR3，滿足車用、工業等客戶長期需求。

其他布局方面，CUBE進度如期，預計2027年進入量產並逐步增加產能；收購英飛凌NOR Flash與F-RAM事業案，則待取得主管機關核准，預計2027年下半年完成交割，交易後將以Spansion為名維持獨立營運，保有自身銷售與設計團隊。對整體市況，華邦電仍留意通膨、利率對消費支出及傳統電子需求的影響，但認為AI需求持續支撐記憶體上升循環，自身獲利動能維持強勁，經營上將重視長期供貨關係，而非單純追求最高價格。

news.Title: European shares falls as Apple margin warning triggers global tech rout
news.Content:
Investing.com - European shares declined on Tuesday, succumbing to a worldwide sell-off across technology bourses after Apple warned of margin compression from rising chip costs, while a $20 billion capital raise by Oracle reignited investor anxiety over artificial intelligence funding and cash burn.

The pan-European STOXX 600 index dropped 0.6%, while Germany's DAX fell 0.3%. France's CAC 40 fell 0.3% while London's FTSE 100 declined 1.1%.

The drawdown was led by the technology sector after Apple warned that persistent inflation in memory chip prices would squeeze gross margins through the crucial holiday shopping quarter.

The continent's semiconductor ecosystem - including lithography giant ASML, assembly equipment makers ASM International and BE SemiconductoR all fell between 2% and 4% and chip suppliers STMicroelectronics and Infineon - trades as a direct proxy for global consumer electronics hardware and datacenter supply chains - fell over 3% each.

With the world's most valuable tech platform signaling that higher component bills are eroding profitability, European semiconductor suppliers came under sharp selling pressure amid fears that hardware makers will either absorb margin compression or face demand destruction if input expenses are passed on to consumers.

The hardware chill was compounded by news that enterprise software giant Oracle plans to raise $20 billion through a combination of bond and share sales to fund its aggressive cloud infrastructure and datacenter expansion.

"Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Tesla and Apple have now all released their latest quarterly results and been met with varying degrees of scepticism, so all eyes are now switching to Nvidia's third-quarter numbers that are due on 17 November," said AJ Bell's investment director, Russ Mould.

This week, about 20% of the STOXX 600 companies are expected to report their quarterly results, marking one of the busiest stretches of the European third-quarter earnings season.

German airline group Lufthansa saw its shares gain 1.6%. The management narrowed its full-year 2026 operating profit forecast due to soaring jet fuel costs tied to Middle Eastern supply tensions.

Conversely, healthcare giants helped cushion tech loses. Dutch medical technology heavyweight Koninklijke Philips advanced 6% after posting higher quarterly profit.

U.S. midterms test Trump's second-term agenda

Cross-asset flows were further restrained by caution ahead of Tuesday's U.S. midterm elections, with American voters heading to the polls to deliver a referendum on the first two years of President Donald Trump's second term.

A Democratic-controlled or divided Congress would introduce legislative gridlock, slowing domestic deregulatory momentum and raising the stakes for upcoming federal debt ceiling negotiations, while potentially curbing federal spending initiatives.

With investors also awaiting Friday's October U.S. nonfarm payrolls report to gauge the Federal Reserve's December interest-rate trajectory, dealing desks maintained low risk profiles across European bourses.

Among other earnings moves, Truecaller fell 17% after the Stockholm-listed caller-identification company reported a third-quarter net loss and issued a cautious outlook on user growth.
